@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=4439 sha256=b3d004b9a40e3f841c04b05819e024521728513d01b5afe1024488c2df2b9c0c path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/BoundedConductorFrontier.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.CompensationLoop

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — the bounded-conductor frontier object (§60)

```
BOUNDED-CONDUCTOR KERNEL (1000 < ell ≤ 5000) : KERNEL-PROVED DEFINITION
BoundedConductorK1Target                      : OPEN  (never inhabited)
FixedConductorCharacterBound                  : OPEN INTERFACE (never inhabited)
CHARACTER BOUND ⇒ k = 1 OWNER BOUND           : KERNEL-PROVED (conditional)
POSITIVE FINITE-KERNEL WRAPPER                : RETIRED_NONCLOSING
```

The current `k = 1` frontier is the **bounded-conductor signed outer-`z` estimate** for the
returned finite-conductor kernel `returnedKernel` of `CompensationLoop` (support
`1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000`).

`BoundedConductorK1Target b` is the OPEN analytic goal "the bounded-conductor kernel is
bounded by `b` uniformly in the physical window".  It is **not inhabited anywhere in this
bank**, and `boundedConductor_target_has_content` records that the underlying kernel is not
the zero object, so the goal is not vacuous.

`FixedConductorCharacterBound b` is the next analytic target: control of the **signed
outer-`z` sum** after a finite DFT/character expansion of the bounded-conductor kernel.  It
is likewise not inhabited; `character_bound_implies_k1_owner_bound` is the exact conditional
reduction at the source level.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §60.1  The OPEN bounded-conductor target -/

/-- **OPEN.**  The bounded-conductor `k = 1` target: a uniform bound `b` for the returned
finite-conductor kernel on `1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000`.  This proposition is *never inhabited* in this
bank. -/
def BoundedConductorK1Target (b : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B z : ℤ, |returnedKernel A B z| ≤ b

/-- **`boundedConductorTarget_mono`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The target is monotone in the
budget. -/
theorem boundedConductorTarget_mono {b b' : ℚ} (h : b ≤ b') (hb : BoundedConductorK1Target b) :
    BoundedConductorK1Target b' :=
  fun A B z => le_trans (hb A B z) h

/-- **`boundedConductor_target_has_content`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The target is not vacuous:
the bounded-conductor kernel is built from atoms that do not all vanish. -/
theorem boundedConductor_target_has_content :
    ∃ ell ∈ Finset.Icc 1001 5000, ∃ s z : ℤ, Kell ell s z ≠ 0 :=
  returnedKernel_not_identically_zero

/-! ## §60.2  The new research interface -/

/-- **OPEN interface.**  `FixedConductorCharacterBound b`: after a finite DFT/character
expansion of the bounded-conductor kernel for `1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000`, the *signed outer-`z` sum*
against any bounded coefficient sequence is controlled by `b`.  Not inhabited. -/
def FixedConductorCharacterBound (b : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A B : ℤ) (Zset : Finset ℤ) (w : ℤ → ℚ), (∀ z, |w z| ≤ 1) →
    |∑ z ∈ Zset, w z * returnedKernel A B z| ≤ b

/-- **`character_bound_implies_k1_owner_bound`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` (conditional).  The signed
outer-`z` character bound implies the corresponding `k = 1` owner bound at the exact source
level: specialise to a single `z` with unit weight. -/
theorem character_bound_implies_k1_owner_bound {b : ℚ}
    (h : FixedConductorCharacterBound b) : BoundedConductorK1Target b := by
  intro A B z
  have hone : ∀ y : ℤ, |(1 : ℚ)| ≤ 1 := fun _ => by norm_num
  have := h A B {z} (fun _ => (1 : ℚ)) hone
  simpa using this

/-! ## §60.3  Retired wrapper -/

/-- Evidence tags used by this module. -/
inductive FrontierStatus
  | kernelProved
  | openGoal
  | retiredNonclosing
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- The positive finite-kernel wrapper is retired: bounding the *absolute values* of the
returned atoms cannot close the signed problem, since the signed cancellation is exactly what
the frontier estimate has to exploit. -/
def positiveFiniteKernelWrapper : FrontierStatus := .retiredNonclosing

/-- The current `k = 1` frontier. -/
def currentK1Frontier : FrontierStatus := .openGoal

/-- **`frontier_status_record`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` (bookkeeping).  The recorded statuses of
the bounded-conductor frontier. -/
theorem frontier_status_record :
    positiveFiniteKernelWrapper = FrontierStatus.retiredNonclosing ∧
      currentK1Frontier = FrontierStatus.openGoal ∧
      currentK1Frontier ≠ FrontierStatus.kernelProved :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, by decide⟩

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=21792 sha256=01084163db2c16e5144c1ebb32bd957c84b6345c5a03cc8234030f3715fd479a path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/BoundedConductorTargetAudit.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.FixedConductorCharacterRepair
import RequestProject.Erdos287.SmallEllMeanCovariance

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — audit of the bounded-conductor `k = 1` target (§62)

```
LONG-WINDOW PERIOD LAW                       : KERNEL-PROVED
returnedKernel 0 (P·n) 1 = n·P·meanSum       : KERNEL-PROVED
meanSum ≠ 0  (4999-adic valuation)           : KERNEL-PROVED
BoundedConductorK1Target AS STATED           : KERNEL-REFUTED
```

`BoundedConductorFrontier` states the `k = 1` frontier target as

    BoundedConductorK1Target b : ∀ A B z, |returnedKernel A B z| ≤ b,

i.e. a *uniform* bound on the returned finite-conductor kernel over **all** half-open
windows `[A,B)`.  This module audits that statement.

The returned kernel is a window sum of the `ℓ`-periodic local kernels
`K_ℓ (1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000)`, so on a window whose length is a common multiple `P` of all those
periods it is exactly `P · meanSum`, where

    meanSum = ∑_{1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000} meanK ℓ = − ∑_{1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000} μ(ℓ)β(ℓ)/ℓ

is the aggregate complete-period mean already banked in `SmallEllMeanCovariance`.  Taking
`n` consecutive periods multiplies this by `n`, so the target is bounded **iff** the
aggregate mean vanishes.  It does not: the conductor `ℓ = 4999` is prime, contributes
`1/(4999·4997)`, and no other term of the sum has `4999` in its denominator, so the
`4999`-adic valuation of `meanSum` is exactly `−1`.

Consequently `BoundedConductorK1Target b` is **false for every budget `b`**, and — via
`characterMeanBound_iff_boundedConductorTarget` — so is the repaired normalised character
interface.  The bounded-conductor frontier therefore has to be restated over the *physical*
hyperbola windows (a bounded family of windows), not over all half-open windows: an
unrestricted window family carries the nonzero density term `P·meanSum`, which is exactly
the density (`D_X`) owner that `DensityCompensationRestoration.DX_term_not_removable`
already shows cannot be dropped.

Nothing here closes any owner: this is a *negative* audit result about the current
formalisation of the frontier target.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §62.1  Generic periodic window algebra -/

/-- Shift-invariance by a multiple of the period. -/
lemma periodic_shift_nat {f : ℤ → ℚ} {m : ℕ} (hper : ∀ s, f (s + m) = f s) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (s : ℤ), f (s + (m : ℤ) * (k : ℤ)) = f s := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => intro s; simp
  | succ n ih =>
      intro s
      have h1 : s + (m : ℤ) * ((n : ℤ) + 1) = (s + (m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) + (m : ℤ) := by ring
      push_cast
      rw [h1, hper, ih]

/-- A sum over `[0, m·n)` of an `m`-periodic function is `n` copies of the period sum. -/
lemma sum_Ico_period_multiple {f : ℤ → ℚ} {m : ℕ} (hper : ∀ s, f (s + m) = f s) (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)), f s
      = (n : ℚ) * ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (m : ℤ), f s := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have hsplit : Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) ((m : ℤ) * ((n : ℤ) + 1))
          = Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) ∪
              Finset.Ico ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) ((m : ℤ) * ((n : ℤ) + 1)) := by
        rw [Finset.Ico_union_Ico_eq_Ico] <;> nlinarith [Int.natCast_nonneg m, Int.natCast_nonneg n]
      have hdisj : Disjoint (Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)))
          (Finset.Ico ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) ((m : ℤ) * ((n : ℤ) + 1))) :=
        Finset.Ico_disjoint_Ico_consecutive _ _ _
      have htail : ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) ((m : ℤ) * ((n : ℤ) + 1)), f s
          = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (m : ℤ), f s := by
        have hmap : Finset.Ico ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) ((m : ℤ) * ((n : ℤ) + 1))
            = (Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (m : ℤ)).map
                (addLeftEmbedding ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ))) := by
          rw [Finset.map_add_left_Ico]
          congr 1
        rw [hmap, Finset.sum_map]
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => ?_
        have : (addLeftEmbedding ((m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ))) s = s + (m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ) := by
          simp [addLeftEmbedding, add_comm]
        rw [this, periodic_shift_nat hper n s]
      push_cast
      rw [hsplit, Finset.sum_union hdisj, htail, ih]
      ring

/-- The `ℤ`-window `[0, n)` sum equals the `range n` sum. -/
lemma sum_Ico_eq_sum_range (f : ℤ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (n : ℤ), f s = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, f (i : ℤ) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have h1 : ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
      have hins : Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) ((n : ℤ) + 1) = insert (n : ℤ) (Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (n : ℤ)) := by
        ext s
        simp only [Finset.mem_Ico, Finset.mem_insert]
        omega
      have hnot : (n : ℤ) ∉ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (n : ℤ) := by simp
      rw [h1, hins, Finset.sum_insert hnot, ih, Finset.sum_range_succ]
      ring

/-! ## §62.2  The aggregate complete-period mean -/

/-- The conductor range of the returned finite-conductor kernel. -/
def conductorRange : Finset ℕ := Finset.Icc 1001 5000

/-- The complete-period mean of the local kernel `K_ℓ` at the outer point `z = 1`. -/
def meanTerm (ell : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  - ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius ell : ℤ) : ℚ) * beta ell / (ell : ℚ)

/-- The aggregate complete-period mean of the returned finite-conductor kernel. -/
def meanSum : ℚ := ∑ ell ∈ conductorRange, meanTerm ell

/-- Non-squarefree conductors contribute nothing: `μ(ℓ) = 0` kills the whole local kernel. -/
lemma Kell_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree {ell : ℕ} (h : ¬ Squarefree ell) (s z : ℤ) :
    Kell ell s z = 0 := by
  have hmu : ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius ell : ℤ) : ℚ) = 0 := by
    have := (ArithmeticFunction.moebius_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree h)
    exact_mod_cast congrArg (fun x : ℤ => (x : ℚ)) this
  have hc : cEll ell = 0 := by rw [cEll, hmu]; simp
  rw [Kell, hc]; ring

/-- **`meanK_eq_meanTerm`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For every conductor `ℓ > 1` the complete-period
mean at `z = 1` is `−μ(ℓ)β(ℓ)/ℓ` (both sides vanish when `ℓ` is not squarefree). -/
theorem meanK_eq_meanTerm {ell : ℕ} (hell : 1 < ell) : meanK ell 1 = meanTerm ell := by
  by_cases hsq : Squarefree ell
  · have hz : ∀ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ¬ p ∣ 1 := by
      intro p hp hdvd
      have := (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp).one_lt
      have := Nat.le_of_dvd one_pos hdvd
      omega
    rw [smallEll_local_mean hsq hell hz, meanTerm]
  · have hzero : periodSum ell 1 = 0 :=
      Finset.sum_eq_zero fun s _ => Kell_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree hsq _ _
    have hmu : ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius ell : ℤ) : ℚ) = 0 := by
      have := ArithmeticFunction.moebius_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree hsq
      exact_mod_cast congrArg (fun x : ℤ => (x : ℚ)) this
    rw [meanK, hzero, meanTerm, hmu]
    simp

/-- **`periodSum_eq_mul_meanTerm`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`. -/
theorem periodSum_eq_mul_meanTerm {ell : ℕ} (hell : 1 < ell) :
    periodSum ell 1 = (ell : ℚ) * meanTerm ell := by
  have h := meanK_eq_meanTerm hell
  rw [meanK] at h
  have hne : (ell : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  field_simp at h
  linarith [h]

/-! ## §62.3  The long-window period law -/

/-- The common period used for the returned kernel: every conductor `ℓ ≤ 5000` divides it. -/
def bigPeriod : ℕ := Nat.factorial 5000

lemma conductor_dvd_bigPeriod {ell : ℕ} (h1 : 1 ≤ ell) (h2 : ell ≤ 5000) : ell ∣ bigPeriod :=
  Nat.dvd_factorial h1 h2

lemma bigPeriod_pos : 0 < bigPeriod := Nat.factorial_pos 5000

/-- **`Kell_long_window`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The window sum of `K_ℓ` over `n` full periods
`[0, P·n)` is `P·n·meanTerm ℓ`. -/
theorem Kell_long_window {ell : ℕ} (h1 : 1001 ≤ ell) (h2 : ell ≤ 5000) (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) ((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)), Kell ell s 1
      = (bigPeriod : ℚ) * (n : ℚ) * meanTerm ell := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := conductor_dvd_bigPeriod (by omega) h2
  have hper : ∀ s : ℤ, Kell ell (s + ell) 1 = Kell ell s 1 := fun s => Kell_periodic ell s 1
  have hrw : (bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ) = (ell : ℤ) * ((c * n : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
    rw [hc]; push_cast; ring
  rw [hrw, sum_Ico_period_multiple hper (c * n), sum_Ico_eq_sum_range]
  have hps : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range ell, Kell ell (i : ℤ) 1 = periodSum ell 1 := by
    rw [periodSum]; norm_num
  rw [hps, periodSum_eq_mul_meanTerm (by omega)]
  rw [hc]; push_cast; ring

/-- **`returnedKernel_long_window`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Over `n` full periods the returned
finite-conductor kernel is exactly `P·n·meanSum`. -/
theorem returnedKernel_long_window (n : ℕ) :
    returnedKernel 0 ((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) 1
      = (bigPeriod : ℚ) * (n : ℚ) * meanSum := by
  have hstep : ∀ ell ∈ conductorRange,
      Qell ell 0 ((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) 1 = (bigPeriod : ℚ) * (n : ℚ) * meanTerm ell := by
    intro ell hell
    rw [conductorRange, Finset.mem_Icc] at hell
    rw [← Qell_compiler (by omega : 0 < ell)]
    exact Kell_long_window hell.1 hell.2 n
  rw [returnedKernel, show Finset.Icc 1001 5000 = conductorRange from rfl,
    Finset.sum_congr rfl hstep, meanSum, Finset.mul_sum]

/-! ## §62.4  The aggregate mean does not vanish -/

/-- The natural-number denominator of the term at a squarefree odd conductor. -/
def meanDen (ell : ℕ) : ℕ := ell * ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, (p - 2)

lemma prod_sub_two_cast (ell : ℕ) :
    ((∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, (p - 2) : ℕ) : ℚ) = ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) - 2) := by
  rw [Nat.cast_prod]
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun p hp => ?_
  have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp).two_le
  rw [Nat.cast_sub hp2]
  norm_num

/-- Away from squarefree odd conductors the term vanishes. -/
lemma meanTerm_eq_zero {ell : ℕ} (h : ¬ (Squarefree ell ∧ ¬ 2 ∣ ell)) : meanTerm ell = 0 := by
  rw [meanTerm, beta, if_neg h]
  simp

/-- At a squarefree odd conductor the term is `−μ(ℓ)` over the natural denominator
`ℓ·∏_{p∣ℓ}(p−2)`. -/
lemma meanTerm_eq_div {ell : ℕ} (hsq : Squarefree ell) (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ ell) :
    meanTerm ell = ((- (ArithmeticFunction.moebius ell) : ℤ) : ℚ) / ((meanDen ell : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
  rw [meanTerm, beta, if_pos ⟨hsq, hodd⟩, meanDen, Nat.cast_mul, prod_sub_two_cast]
  push_cast
  rw [div_eq_mul_inv, div_eq_mul_inv, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_inv, one_mul]
  ring

lemma meanDen_ne_zero {ell : ℕ} (hell : 0 < ell) (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ ell) : meanDen ell ≠ 0 := by
  rw [meanDen]
  refine Nat.mul_ne_zero hell.ne' (Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.2 fun p hp => ?_)
  have hpp : p.Prime := Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp
  have hpd : p ∣ ell := Nat.dvd_of_mem_primeFactors hp
  have hp2 : p ≠ 2 := fun h => hodd (h ▸ hpd)
  have := hpp.two_le
  omega

/-- The prime `4999` does not divide the denominator of any other term in range. -/
lemma not_dvd_meanDen {ell : ℕ} (h1 : 1001 ≤ ell) (h2 : ell ≤ 5000) (hne : ell ≠ 4999)
    (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ ell) : ¬ (4999 ∣ meanDen ell) := by
  have hp : Nat.Prime 4999 := by norm_num
  intro hdvd
  rw [meanDen] at hdvd
  rcases (Nat.Prime.dvd_mul hp).1 hdvd with hell | hprod
  · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hell
    clear hdvd hodd hp
    omega
  · obtain ⟨q, hq, hqd⟩ := Prime.exists_mem_finset_dvd hp.prime hprod
    have hqp : q.Prime := Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hq
    have hqe : q ∣ ell := Nat.dvd_of_mem_primeFactors hq
    have hq2 : q ≠ 2 := fun h => hodd (h ▸ hqe)
    have hq3 : 3 ≤ q := by have := hqp.two_le; omega
    have hqle : q ≤ ell := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) hqe
    have hle2 := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) hqd
    clear hdvd hprod hqd hqe hq2 hqp hq hp hodd
    omega

lemma meanDen_4999 : meanDen 4999 = 4999 * 4997 := by
  have hp : Nat.Prime 4999 := by norm_num
  rw [meanDen, hp.primeFactors, Finset.prod_singleton]

/-- **`padicNorm_meanTerm_le_one`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Every conductor other than `4999`
contributes a `4999`-adic integer. -/
lemma padicNorm_meanTerm_le_one {ell : ℕ} (h1 : 1001 ≤ ell) (h2 : ell ≤ 5000)
    (hne : ell ≠ 4999) : padicNorm 4999 (meanTerm ell) ≤ 1 := by
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 4999) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
  by_cases hgood : Squarefree ell ∧ ¬ 2 ∣ ell
  · obtain ⟨hsq, hodd⟩ := hgood
    have hden : ¬ ((4999 : ℤ) ∣ ((meanDen ell : ℕ) : ℤ)) := by
      intro h
      exact not_dvd_meanDen h1 h2 hne hodd (by exact_mod_cast h)
    have hnorm_den : padicNorm 4999 (((meanDen ell : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℚ) = 1 :=
      (padicNorm.int_eq_one_iff _).2 hden
    rw [meanTerm_eq_div hsq hodd, padicNorm.div]
    have hnum : padicNorm 4999 (((- (ArithmeticFunction.moebius ell) : ℤ)) : ℚ) ≤ 1 :=
      padicNorm.of_int _
    have hcast : (((meanDen ell : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℚ) = ((meanDen ell : ℕ) : ℚ) := by push_cast; ring
    rw [hcast] at hnorm_den
    rw [hnorm_den, div_one]
    exact hnum
  · rw [meanTerm_eq_zero hgood, padicNorm.zero]
    norm_num

/-- **`padicNorm_meanTerm_4999`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The conductor `4999` contributes a term
of `4999`-adic norm strictly larger than `1` (valuation `−1`). -/
lemma padicNorm_meanTerm_4999 : 1 < padicNorm 4999 (meanTerm 4999) := by
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 4999) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
  have hp : Nat.Prime 4999 := by norm_num
  have hsq : Squarefree (4999 : ℕ) := hp.squarefree
  have hodd : ¬ (2 ∣ (4999 : ℕ)) := by norm_num
  have hmu : ArithmeticFunction.moebius 4999 = -1 := by
    rw [ArithmeticFunction.moebius_apply_prime hp]
  have hnum : ((- (ArithmeticFunction.moebius 4999) : ℤ) : ℚ) = 1 := by
    rw [hmu]; norm_num
  have hDpos : (0 : ℚ) < ((meanDen 4999 : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
    rw [meanDen_4999]; norm_num
  have hDdvd : ((4999 : ℤ)) ∣ (((meanDen 4999 : ℕ)) : ℤ) := by
    rw [meanDen_4999]; norm_num
  have hlt : padicNorm 4999 ((((meanDen 4999 : ℕ)) : ℤ) : ℚ) < 1 :=
    (padicNorm.int_lt_one_iff _).2 hDdvd
  have hne0 : padicNorm 4999 ((((meanDen 4999 : ℕ)) : ℤ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    refine padicNorm.nonzero ?_
    push_cast
    exact hDpos.ne'
  have hpos : 0 < padicNorm 4999 ((((meanDen 4999 : ℕ)) : ℤ) : ℚ) :=
    lt_of_le_of_ne (padicNorm.nonneg _) (Ne.symm hne0)
  rw [meanTerm_eq_div hsq hodd, padicNorm.div, hnum, padicNorm.one]
  have hcast : (((meanDen 4999 : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℚ) = ((meanDen 4999 : ℕ) : ℚ) := by push_cast; ring
  rw [hcast] at hlt hpos
  rw [one_lt_div hpos]
  exact hlt

/-- **`meanSum_ne_zero`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The aggregate complete-period mean of the
returned finite-conductor kernel is nonzero: its `4999`-adic valuation is `−1`, because the
prime conductor `ℓ = 4999` contributes `1/(4999·4997)` and no other conductor in the range
carries `4999` in its denominator. -/
theorem meanSum_ne_zero : meanSum ≠ 0 := by
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 4999) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
  intro hzero
  have hmem : (4999 : ℕ) ∈ conductorRange := by
    rw [conductorRange, Finset.mem_Icc]; omega
  have hsplit : meanTerm 4999 + ∑ ell ∈ conductorRange.erase 4999, meanTerm ell = meanSum :=
    Finset.add_sum_erase _ _ hmem
  have hrest : padicNorm 4999 (∑ ell ∈ conductorRange.erase 4999, meanTerm ell) ≤ 1 := by
    refine padicNorm.sum_le' (fun ell hell => ?_) (by norm_num)
    have hne : ell ≠ 4999 := Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hell
    have hmem' := Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hell
    rw [conductorRange, Finset.mem_Icc] at hmem'
    exact padicNorm_meanTerm_le_one hmem'.1 hmem'.2 hne
  have heq : meanTerm 4999 = -(∑ ell ∈ conductorRange.erase 4999, meanTerm ell) := by
    rw [hzero] at hsplit; linarith
  have hbig := padicNorm_meanTerm_4999
  rw [heq, padicNorm.neg] at hbig
  linarith

/-! ## §62.5  The frontier target as stated is false -/

/-- **`boundedConductorK1Target_unsatisfiable`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The `k = 1` frontier
target, as currently formalised (a uniform bound over *all* half-open windows), is false for
every budget `b`. -/
theorem boundedConductorK1Target_unsatisfiable (b : ℚ) : ¬ BoundedConductorK1Target b := by
  intro h
  have hP : (0 : ℚ) < (bigPeriod : ℚ) := Nat.cast_pos.2 bigPeriod_pos
  have hm : 0 < |meanSum| := abs_pos.2 meanSum_ne_zero
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt (b / ((bigPeriod : ℚ) * |meanSum|))
  have hpos : 0 < (bigPeriod : ℚ) * |meanSum| := mul_pos hP hm
  have hbig : b < (n : ℚ) * ((bigPeriod : ℚ) * |meanSum|) := by
    rw [div_lt_iff₀ hpos] at hn; linarith
  have hle := h 0 ((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) 1
  have habs : |(bigPeriod : ℚ) * (n : ℚ) * meanSum|
      = (n : ℚ) * ((bigPeriod : ℚ) * |meanSum|) := by
    rw [abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg hP.le, abs_of_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg (α := ℚ) n)]
    ring
  rw [returnedKernel_long_window n, habs] at hle
  linarith

/-- **`characterMeanBound_unsatisfiable`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Hence even the *normalised*
character interface of §61 is unsatisfiable, since it is equivalent to the target. -/
theorem characterMeanBound_unsatisfiable (b : ℚ) : ¬ FixedConductorCharacterMeanBound b :=
  fun h => boundedConductorK1Target_unsatisfiable b
    ((characterMeanBound_iff_boundedConductorTarget b).1 h)

/-! ## §62.6  The density-centred replacement target -/

/-- The complete-period sum of `K_ℓ` at an arbitrary outer point `z`. -/
def perSum (ell : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : ℚ := ∑ s ∈ Finset.range ell, Kell ell (s : ℤ) z

/-- The complete-period mean of `K_ℓ` at an arbitrary outer point `z`. -/
def perMean (ell : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : ℚ := perSum ell z / (ell : ℚ)

/-- The aggregate complete-period mean of the returned kernel at the outer point `z`. -/
def meanSumAt (z : ℤ) : ℚ := ∑ ell ∈ conductorRange, perMean ell z

lemma perSum_one (ell : ℕ) : perSum ell 1 = periodSum ell 1 := by
  rw [perSum, periodSum]
  norm_num

lemma perMean_one (ell : ℕ) : perMean ell 1 = meanK ell 1 := by
  rw [perMean, meanK, perSum_one]

/-- **`meanSumAt_one`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  At `z = 1` the aggregate mean is `meanSum`. -/
theorem meanSumAt_one : meanSumAt 1 = meanSum := by
  rw [meanSumAt, meanSum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ell hell => ?_
  rw [conductorRange, Finset.mem_Icc] at hell
  rw [perMean_one, meanK_eq_meanTerm (by omega)]

/-- **Repaired frontier target.**  The bounded-conductor `k = 1` target with the exact
density term `(B − A)·meanSumAt z` subtracted, on ordered windows.  This is the statement
that survives the audit of §62.5: the unnormalised target fails only through the density
(`D_X`) owner, which `DensityCompensationRestoration.DX_term_not_removable` already
identifies as non-removable. -/
def CentredBoundedConductorK1Target (b : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B z : ℤ, A ≤ B → |returnedKernel A B z - ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) * meanSumAt z| ≤ b

/-- **`returnedKernel_of_empty_window`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  On a degenerate window the
returned kernel vanishes. -/
theorem returnedKernel_of_empty_window {A B : ℤ} (h : B ≤ A) (z : ℤ) :
    returnedKernel A B z = 0 := by
  refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun ell hell => ?_
  rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at hell
  rw [← Qell_compiler (by omega : 0 < ell)]
  refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun s hs => ?_
  rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hs
  omega

/-- **`centred_target_needs_ordered_windows`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The restriction `A ≤ B` in
the centred target is *necessary*: on degenerate windows the kernel is `0` while the density
term is unbounded, so the unrestricted centred statement is false for every budget. -/
theorem centred_target_needs_ordered_windows (b : ℚ) :
    ¬ (∀ A B z : ℤ, |returnedKernel A B z - ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) * meanSumAt z| ≤ b) := by
  intro h
  have hm : 0 < |meanSum| := abs_pos.2 meanSum_ne_zero
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt (b / |meanSum|)
  have hbig : b < (n : ℚ) * |meanSum| := by
    rw [div_lt_iff₀ hm] at hn; linarith
  have hle := h 0 (-(n : ℤ)) 1
  rw [returnedKernel_of_empty_window (by omega : -(n : ℤ) ≤ 0) 1, meanSumAt_one] at hle
  have hcast : ((-(n : ℤ) - 0 : ℤ) : ℚ) = -(n : ℚ) := by push_cast; ring
  rw [hcast, zero_sub, abs_neg, abs_mul, abs_neg,
    abs_of_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg (α := ℚ) n)] at hle
  linarith

/-- **`centred_kernel_vanishes_on_full_periods`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The long-window
counterexample of §62.5 does *not* refute the centred target: on `n` full periods the centred
kernel is exactly `0`, i.e. the subtracted density term is exactly the obstruction found. -/
theorem centred_kernel_vanishes_on_full_periods (n : ℕ) :
    returnedKernel 0 ((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) 1
        - (((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ) - 0 : ℤ) : ℚ) * meanSumAt 1 = 0 := by
  rw [returnedKernel_long_window n, meanSumAt_one]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- **`frontier_repair_summary`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping.  (i) the unnormalised
character interface is false; (ii) the pointwise `k = 1` target is false; (iii) the normalised
character interface is false; and (iv) the density-centred replacement target is not refuted
by the long-window witness.  Nothing here inhabits an open target. -/
theorem frontier_repair_summary (b : ℚ) :
    (¬ FixedConductorCharacterBound b) ∧ (¬ BoundedConductorK1Target b) ∧
      (¬ FixedConductorCharacterMeanBound b) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, returnedKernel 0 ((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) 1
        - (((bigPeriod : ℤ) * (n : ℤ) - 0 : ℤ) : ℚ) * meanSumAt 1 = 0) :=
  ⟨fixedConductorCharacterBound_unsatisfiable b, boundedConductorK1Target_unsatisfiable b,
    characterMeanBound_unsatisfiable b, centred_kernel_vanishes_on_full_periods⟩

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

import Mathlib

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — physical `B_src` normalisation (§2)

```
PHYSICAL B1 NORMALIZATION : KERNEL-PROVED
B0 MULTIPLICATIVITY       : KERNEL-PROVED
beta MULTIPLICATIVITY     : KERNEL-PROVED
B1-ONCE FIREWALL          : KERNEL-PROVED
```

The physical normalisation carries the global constant `B1` **once**:

    B0(n) = ∏_{p ∣ n, p > 2} (p−1)/(p−2),      B(n) = B1 · B0(n),

    β(k)  = μ(k)² · 1_{2 ∤ k} / ∏_{p ∣ k} (p − 2).

`B0` and `β` are multiplicative on coprime arguments; `B` is **not** — the
correct typed relation is `B1 · B(ab) = B(a)·B(b)`, and
`B1_onceFirewall` records the concrete failure of the "one `B1` per prime
factor" normalisation.

Everything in this file is finite: products range over `Nat.primeFactors`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset ArithmeticFunction

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §2.1  Definitions -/

/-- The odd prime factors of `n`. -/
def oddPrimeFactors (n : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := n.primeFactors.erase 2

lemma mem_oddPrimeFactors {n p : ℕ} :
    p ∈ oddPrimeFactors n ↔ p ≠ 2 ∧ p ∈ n.primeFactors := by
  simp [oddPrimeFactors]

lemma oddPrimeFactors_prime {n p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ oddPrimeFactors n) : p.Prime :=
  Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors (mem_oddPrimeFactors.1 hp).2

lemma oddPrimeFactors_ne_two {n p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ oddPrimeFactors n) : p ≠ 2 :=
  (mem_oddPrimeFactors.1 hp).1

/-- For `p` an odd prime, `(p : ℚ) − 2 ≠ 0`. -/
lemma sub_two_ne_zero {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h2 : p ≠ 2) : ((p : ℚ) - 2) ≠ 0 := by
  have h3 : 3 ≤ p := by have := hp.two_le; omega
  have : (3 : ℚ) ≤ (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast h3
  intro h; linarith [sub_eq_zero.1 h]

/-- `B0(n) = ∏_{p ∣ n, p > 2} (p−1)/(p−2)`, the normalised local factor. -/
def B0 (n : ℕ) : ℚ := ∏ p ∈ oddPrimeFactors n, (((p : ℚ) - 1) / ((p : ℚ) - 2))

/-- `B(n) = B1 · B0(n)`: the physical source weight, with the global constant `B1`
appearing **exactly once**. -/
def B (B1 : ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ := B1 * B0 n

/-- `β(k) = μ(k)² 1_{2∤k} / ∏_{p ∣ k}(p−2)`. -/
def beta (k : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  (if Squarefree k ∧ ¬ (2 ∣ k) then (1 : ℚ) else 0) / ∏ p ∈ k.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) - 2)

@[simp] lemma B0_one : B0 1 = 1 := by simp [B0, oddPrimeFactors]

@[simp] lemma B_one (B1 : ℚ) : B B1 1 = B1 := by simp [B]

@[simp] lemma beta_one : beta 1 = 1 := by simp [beta]

@[simp] lemma beta_zero : beta 0 = 0 := by
  simp [beta]

lemma beta_eq_zero_of_even {k : ℕ} (h : 2 ∣ k) : beta k = 0 := by
  simp [beta, h]

lemma beta_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree {k : ℕ} (h : ¬ Squarefree k) : beta k = 0 := by
  simp [beta, h]

/-- On an odd squarefree argument `β` is the reciprocal of `∏ (p−2)`. -/
lemma beta_of_odd_squarefree {k : ℕ} (hsq : Squarefree k) (hodd : ¬ (2 ∣ k)) :
    beta k = 1 / ∏ p ∈ k.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) - 2) := by
  simp [beta, hsq, hodd]

/-- `β` at an odd prime. -/
lemma beta_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h2 : p ≠ 2) : beta p = 1 / ((p : ℚ) - 2) := by
  rw [beta_of_odd_squarefree hp.squarefree (by
        intro h
        exact h2 ((Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq Nat.prime_two hp).1 h).symm),
    hp.primeFactors, Finset.prod_singleton]

/-- `B0` at an odd prime. -/
lemma B0_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h2 : p ≠ 2) :
    B0 p = ((p : ℚ) - 1) / ((p : ℚ) - 2) := by
  rw [B0, oddPrimeFactors, hp.primeFactors, Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem (by simpa using Ne.symm h2),
    Finset.prod_singleton]

/-! ## §2.2  Multiplicativity -/

lemma oddPrimeFactors_mul {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    oddPrimeFactors (a * b) = oddPrimeFactors a ∪ oddPrimeFactors b := by
  simp [oddPrimeFactors, Nat.primeFactors_mul ha hb, Finset.erase_union_distrib]

/-- **`B0_mul`.** `B0` is multiplicative on coprime nonzero arguments. -/
theorem B0_mul {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    B0 (a * b) = B0 a * B0 b := by
  rw [B0, B0, B0, oddPrimeFactors_mul ha hb, Finset.prod_union]
  refine Finset.disjoint_left.2 fun p hpa hpb => ?_
  exact (Finset.disjoint_left.1 hab.disjoint_primeFactors
    (mem_oddPrimeFactors.1 hpa).2) (mem_oddPrimeFactors.1 hpb).2

/-- **`beta_mul`.** `β` is multiplicative on coprime nonzero arguments. -/
theorem beta_mul {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    beta (a * b) = beta a * beta b := by
  have hprod : ∏ p ∈ (a * b).primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) - 2)
      = (∏ p ∈ a.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) - 2)) * ∏ p ∈ b.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) - 2) := by
    rw [Nat.primeFactors_mul ha hb, Finset.prod_union hab.disjoint_primeFactors]
  by_cases hsq : Squarefree (a * b)
  · have hsa : Squarefree a := hsq.of_mul_left
    have hsb : Squarefree b := hsq.of_mul_right
    by_cases h2 : 2 ∣ a * b
    · rcases (Nat.Prime.dvd_mul Nat.prime_two).1 h2 with h | h
      · rw [beta_eq_zero_of_even h2, beta_eq_zero_of_even h, zero_mul]
      · rw [beta_eq_zero_of_even h2, beta_eq_zero_of_even h, mul_zero]
    · have h2a : ¬ (2 ∣ a) := fun h => h2 (h.mul_right b)
      have h2b : ¬ (2 ∣ b) := fun h => h2 (Dvd.dvd.mul_left h a)
      rw [beta_of_odd_squarefree hsq h2, beta_of_odd_squarefree hsa h2a,
        beta_of_odd_squarefree hsb h2b, hprod]
      field_simp
  · have : ¬ Squarefree a ∨ ¬ Squarefree b := by
      by_contra hcon
      push_neg at hcon
      exact hsq ((Nat.squarefree_mul hab).2 ⟨hcon.1, hcon.2⟩)
    rcases this with h | h
    · rw [beta_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree hsq, beta_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree h, zero_mul]
    · rw [beta_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree hsq, beta_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree h, mul_zero]

/-- **`B_mul_typed`.** `B` is *not* multiplicative: the physical relation on coprime
arguments is `B1 · B(ab) = B(a)·B(b)`, i.e. `B1` occurs once. -/
theorem B_mul_typed (B1 : ℚ) {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    B1 * B B1 (a * b) = B B1 a * B B1 b := by
  simp only [B, B0_mul ha hb hab]; ring

/-! ## §2.3  The `B1`-once firewall -/

lemma primeFactors_fifteen : (15 : ℕ).primeFactors = {3, 5} := by
  have h : (15 : ℕ) = 3 * 5 := by norm_num
  rw [h, Nat.primeFactors_mul (by norm_num) (by norm_num),
    Nat.Prime.primeFactors (by norm_num), Nat.Prime.primeFactors (by norm_num)]
  rfl

lemma oddPrimeFactors_fifteen : oddPrimeFactors 15 = {3, 5} := by
  rw [oddPrimeFactors, primeFactors_fifteen]
  decide

@[simp] lemma B0_fifteen : B0 15 = 8 / 3 := by
  rw [B0, oddPrimeFactors_fifteen]; norm_num

/-- **`B1_onceFirewall`.** `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Encoding `B1` once per prime factor is a
genuinely different (wrong) normalisation: at `n = 15` the two disagree for every
`B1 ∉ {0, 1}`. -/
theorem B1_onceFirewall (B1 : ℚ) (h0 : B1 ≠ 0) (h1 : B1 ≠ 1) :
    B B1 15 ≠ B1 ^ 2 * B0 15 := by
  rw [B, B0_fifteen]
  intro h
  have key : B1 * (B1 - 1) = 0 := by nlinarith [h]
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 key with h' | h'
  · exact h0 h'
  · exact h1 (by linarith [sub_eq_zero.1 h'])

/-- `B0` ignores the prime `2`: powers of two carry no odd local factor. -/
@[simp] theorem B0_two_pow (k : ℕ) : B0 (2 ^ k) = 1 := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with rfl | hk
  · simp
  · rw [B0, oddPrimeFactors, Nat.primeFactors_prime_pow hk.ne' Nat.prime_two]
    simp

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=8184 sha256=eb74044e3dd0de56d98e14684b864ca9876f15761f1ede13d8a10e7ab7f86229 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/C1C2Splice.lean@@
import Mathlib

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — the `c = 1 / c = 2` splice (§10, §11)

```
c1/c2 DISCRETE SPLICE   : KERNEL-PROVED
c1/c2 CONTINUOUS SPLICE : KERNEL-PROVED (integrability as an explicit hypothesis)
```

## Conventions

The two lanes are, with `T d n = A_d(n)·W(dn/X)` an arbitrary real weight,

    D₁ = ∑_d μ(d) ∑_{d < n ≤ Nb}       T d n,
    D₂ = ∑_d μ(d) ∑_{2d < m ≤ Nb/2}    T d (2m)      (the `n ↦ 2n` substituted lane),

so that the `c = 2` lane sees exactly the **even** `n > 4d`.  Then

    D₁ − D₂ = ∑_d μ(d) [ ∑_{n > d, n odd} T d n + ∑_{d < n ≤ 4d, n even} T d n ],

and the upper endpoint `4d` is *derived* from the substitution `n ↦ 2n`
(`discrete_splice`).  The continuous lane is the exact mirror,

    C₁ = ∑_d μ(d) M_d ∫_d^∞ W(dt/X) dt,
    C₂ = ∑_d μ(d) M_d ∫_{2d}^∞ W(2dt/X) dt,

and the two factors `1/2` in

    C₁ − C₂ = ∑_d μ(d) M_d [ ½∫_d^∞ W(dt/X)dt + ½∫_d^{4d} W(dt/X)dt ]

come from the substitution `∫_{Ioi 2d} g(2t)dt = ½∫_{Ioi 4d} g`, not from an
assumption (`continuous_splice_pointwise`, `continuous_splice`).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset ArithmeticFunction MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §10  The discrete splice -/

/-- The `c = 1` discrete lane, truncated at `Nb`. -/
def Ddisc1 (T : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (Dset : Finset ℕ) (Nb : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Dset, (moebius d : ℝ) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb, T d n

/-- The `c = 2` discrete lane after the substitution `n ↦ 2n`. -/
def Ddisc2 (T : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (Dset : Finset ℕ) (Nb : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Dset, (moebius d : ℝ) * ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ioc (2 * d) (Nb / 2), T d (2 * m)

/-- The image of `Ioc (2d) B` under doubling is the set of even elements of `Ioc (4d) (2B)`. -/
lemma image_two_mul_Ioc (d B : ℕ) :
    (Finset.Ioc (2 * d) B).image (fun m => 2 * m)
      = (Finset.Ioc (4 * d) (2 * B)).filter (fun n => 2 ∣ n) := by
  ext n
  simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Ioc]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨m, ⟨h1, h2⟩, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩
  · rintro ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩
    exact ⟨m, ⟨by omega, by omega⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The per-`d` discrete splice: the `c = 2` lane removes exactly the even `n > 4d`. -/
lemma discrete_splice_pointwise (T : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) {d Nb B : ℕ} (hNb : Nb = 2 * B)
    (h4d : 4 * d ≤ Nb) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb, T d n) - ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ioc (2 * d) (Nb / 2), T d (2 * m)
      = (∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb with ¬ (2 ∣ n), T d n)
        + ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d (4 * d) with (2 ∣ n), T d n := by
  classical
  have hB : Nb / 2 = B := by omega
  -- the substituted lane is the even part beyond `4d`
  have hsub : (∑ m ∈ Finset.Ioc (2 * d) (Nb / 2), T d (2 * m))
      = ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc (4 * d) Nb with (2 ∣ n), T d n := by
    rw [hB]
    conv_rhs => rw [hNb]
    rw [← image_two_mul_Ioc d B,
      Finset.sum_image (by intro x _ y _ h; simp only [] at h; omega)]
  -- split the `c = 1` lane into odd and even parts
  have hsplit : (∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb, T d n)
      = (∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb with ¬ (2 ∣ n), T d n)
        + ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb with (2 ∣ n), T d n := by
    rw [add_comm]
    exact (Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not _ _ _).symm
  -- split the even part at `4d`
  have hIoc : Finset.Ioc d Nb = Finset.Ioc d (4 * d) ∪ Finset.Ioc (4 * d) Nb :=
    (Finset.Ioc_union_Ioc_eq_Ioc (by omega) h4d).symm
  have hdisj : Disjoint (Finset.Ioc d (4 * d)) (Finset.Ioc (4 * d) Nb) := by
    refine Finset.disjoint_left.2 fun x hx hx' => ?_
    simp only [Finset.mem_Ioc] at hx hx'
    omega
  have heven : (∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb with (2 ∣ n), T d n)
      = (∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d (4 * d) with (2 ∣ n), T d n)
        + ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc (4 * d) Nb with (2 ∣ n), T d n := by
    rw [hIoc, Finset.filter_union, Finset.sum_union]
    exact Finset.disjoint_filter_filter hdisj
  rw [hsub, hsplit, heven]
  ring

/-- **`discrete_splice`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact finite-sum `c = 1 / c = 2` splice,

    D₁ − D₂ = ∑_d μ(d) [ ∑_{d < n ≤ Nb, n odd} T d n + ∑_{d < n ≤ 4d, n even} T d n ].

The upper endpoint `4d` is derived from the substitution `n ↦ 2n`. -/
theorem discrete_splice (T : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (Dset : Finset ℕ) {Nb B : ℕ} (hNb : Nb = 2 * B)
    (h4d : ∀ d ∈ Dset, 4 * d ≤ Nb) :
    Ddisc1 T Dset Nb - Ddisc2 T Dset Nb
      = ∑ d ∈ Dset, (moebius d : ℝ) *
          ((∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d Nb with ¬ (2 ∣ n), T d n)
            + ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc d (4 * d) with (2 ∣ n), T d n) := by
  rw [Ddisc1, Ddisc2, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d hd => ?_
  rw [← mul_sub, discrete_splice_pointwise T hNb (h4d d hd)]

/-! ## §11  The continuous splice -/

/-- **`continuous_splice_pointwise`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The per-`d` continuous splice.
Both factors `1/2` come from the substitution `∫_{Ioi 2d} g(2t) dt = ½ ∫_{Ioi 4d} g`. -/
theorem continuous_splice_pointwise (W : ℝ → ℝ) (X : ℝ) {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hint : IntegrableOn (fun t => W (d * t / X)) (Set.Ioi d)) :
    (∫ t in Set.Ioi d, W (d * t / X)) - ∫ t in Set.Ioi (2 * d), W (2 * d * t / X)
      = (1 / 2) * (∫ t in Set.Ioi d, W (d * t / X))
        + (1 / 2) * ∫ t in Set.Ioc d (4 * d), W (d * t / X) := by
  set g : ℝ → ℝ := fun y => W (d * y / X) with hg
  -- the `c = 2` integral is a scaled copy
  have hscale : (∫ t in Set.Ioi (2 * d), W (2 * d * t / X))
      = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∫ s in Set.Ioi (4 * d), g s := by
    have h1 : (∫ t in Set.Ioi (2 * d), W (2 * d * t / X)) = ∫ t in Set.Ioi (2 * d), g (2 * t) := by
      refine setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi fun t _ => ?_
      simp only [hg]
      ring_nf
    rw [h1, integral_comp_mul_left_Ioi g (2 * d) (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) < 2)]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul]
    norm_num
    ring_nf
  -- split the `c = 1` integral at `4d`
  have hsplit : (∫ t in Set.Ioi d, g t)
      = (∫ t in Set.Ioc d (4 * d), g t) + ∫ t in Set.Ioi (4 * d), g t := by
    have hunion : Set.Ioc d (4 * d) ∪ Set.Ioi (4 * d) = Set.Ioi d :=
      Set.Ioc_union_Ioi_eq_Ioi (by linarith)
    have hdisj : Disjoint (Set.Ioc d (4 * d)) (Set.Ioi (4 * d)) :=
      Set.Ioc_disjoint_Ioi le_rfl
    rw [← hunion] at hint ⊢
    rw [setIntegral_union hdisj measurableSet_Ioi
      (hint.mono_set Set.subset_union_left) (hint.mono_set Set.subset_union_right)]
  rw [hscale]
  have : (∫ s in Set.Ioi (4 * d), g s)
      = (∫ t in Set.Ioi d, g t) - ∫ t in Set.Ioc d (4 * d), g t := by rw [hsplit]; ring
  rw [this]
  simp only [hg]
  ring

/-- The `c = 1` continuous lane. -/
noncomputable def Ccont1 (W : ℝ → ℝ) (X : ℝ) (M : ℕ → ℝ) (Dset : Finset ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Dset, (moebius d : ℝ) * M d * ∫ t in Set.Ioi (d : ℝ), W ((d : ℝ) * t / X)

/-- The `c = 2` continuous lane. -/
noncomputable def Ccont2 (W : ℝ → ℝ) (X : ℝ) (M : ℕ → ℝ) (Dset : Finset ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Dset, (moebius d : ℝ) * M d * ∫ t in Set.Ioi (2 * (d : ℝ)), W (2 * (d : ℝ) * t / X)

/-- **`continuous_splice`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` (given integrability of each lane).

    C₁ − C₂ = ∑_d μ(d) M_d [ ½ ∫_d^∞ W(dt/X)dt + ½ ∫_d^{4d} W(dt/X)dt ]. -/
theorem continuous_splice (W : ℝ → ℝ) (X : ℝ) (M : ℕ → ℝ) (Dset : Finset ℕ)
    (hpos : ∀ d ∈ Dset, 0 < d)
    (hint : ∀ d ∈ Dset, IntegrableOn (fun t => W ((d : ℝ) * t / X)) (Set.Ioi (d : ℝ))) :
    Ccont1 W X M Dset - Ccont2 W X M Dset
      = ∑ d ∈ Dset, (moebius d : ℝ) * M d *
          ((1 / 2) * (∫ t in Set.Ioi (d : ℝ), W ((d : ℝ) * t / X))
            + (1 / 2) * ∫ t in Set.Ioc (d : ℝ) (4 * (d : ℝ)), W ((d : ℝ) * t / X)) := by
  rw [Ccont1, Ccont2, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d hd => ?_
  have hd0 : (0 : ℝ) < (d : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hpos d hd
  rw [← mul_sub, continuous_splice_pointwise W X hd0 (hint d hd)]

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=13134 sha256=5b03d651c1aa183d9c2f379c9ef89ccbefa6b65e9db91c4892cdeeccfa0f725e path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/CeilingCRT.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Blocker

/-!
# Erdős Problem #287 — the Ceiling–CRT Pairing package and Large-Ceiling reduction

For a gap-`≤2` counterexample `A` with endpoints `N, M` and a prime `p`, let
`eₚ = maxₐ vₚ(a)` (the top `p`-adic exponent) and set the **ceiling modulus**
`qₚ = p^(eₚ + 1)`.  Since `eₚ` is the maximal `p`-adic valuation, no element of `A`
is divisible by `qₚ`; every multiple of `qₚ` in the window `[N, M]` is a *hole*.

The main results:

* `Gap2CE.ceilingMultiples_are_holes` — any multiple of `qₚ` in `[N, M]` is not in `A`.
* `Gap2CE.HoleForcing` — the abstract property "every multiple of `Q` in `[N,M]` is a hole".
* `exists_crt_adjacent` — the CRT interval-residue lemma.
* `Gap2CE.coprimeHoleModuli_CRT_pair` — two coprime positive hole-forcing moduli
  `Q₁, Q₂` with `Q₁·Q₂ ≤ M - N` produce two adjacent holes, hence a contradiction.
* `Gap2CE.ceilingCRT_pairing` — for distinct primes `p, r`, `qₚ·q_r > M - N`.
* `Gap2CE.atMostOne_small_ceiling` — at most one prime `p` has `qₚ² ≤ M - N`.
* `Gap2CE.AP_prime_kills_minCeil` — for `M ≥ 8152`, no prime `ℓ ∈ [N+1, M-1]` is
  `≡ 1 (mod Q)` where `Q = minₚ qₚ`.
* `Gap2CE.LargeCeilingReduction` — the packaged reduction.

No claim that #287 is solved; only the elementary CRT-pairing structure is certified.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287

namespace Gap2CE

variable (ce : Gap2CE)

/-- The **ceiling modulus** `qₚ = p^(eₚ + 1)`, where `eₚ = maxₐ vₚ(a)` is the top
`p`-adic exponent over `A`. -/
def ceilMod (p : ℕ) : ℕ := p ^ (topExp ce.A p + 1)

/-- The ceiling modulus is positive for a prime base. -/
theorem one_le_ceilMod {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : 1 ≤ ce.ceilMod p := by
  exact Nat.one_le_pow _ _ hp.pos

/-- **Ceiling multiples are holes (Target 1).** If `p` is prime, `x ∈ [N, M]`, and
`qₚ ∣ x`, then `x ∉ A`.

(The hypothesis `x ∈ [N, M]` is requested by the problem statement so that `x` is
literally a hole *in the window*; the divisibility alone already forces `x ∉ A`.) -/
theorem ceilingMultiples_are_holes {p x : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hx : x ∈ Finset.Icc ce.N ce.M) (hdvd : ce.ceilMod p ∣ x) : x ∉ ce.A := by
  contrapose! hdvd;
  unfold ceilMod;
  rw [ Nat.Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization ] <;> norm_num;
  · exact Finset.le_sup ( f := fun a => Nat.factorization a p ) hdvd;
  · assumption;
  · linarith [ Finset.mem_Icc.mp hx, ce.hpos x hdvd ]

/-! ## Abstract hole-forcing moduli -/

/-- `Q` is **hole-forcing** if every multiple of `Q` inside the window `[N, M]`
is absent from `A`. -/
def HoleForcing (Q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, x ∈ Finset.Icc ce.N ce.M → Q ∣ x → x ∉ ce.A

/-- Each ceiling modulus of a prime is hole-forcing (immediate from
`ceilingMultiples_are_holes`). -/
theorem holeForcing_ceilMod {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : ce.HoleForcing (ce.ceilMod p) :=
  fun x hx hdvd => ce.ceilingMultiples_are_holes hp hx hdvd

end Gap2CE

/-- **CRT interval-residue lemma.** Given coprime `Q₁, Q₂ ≥ 1` with `Q₁·Q₂ ≤ M - N`,
there is an `x` with `N ≤ x`, `x + 1 ≤ M`, `Q₁ ∣ x`, and `Q₂ ∣ (x+1)`.

(Any interval of length at least `Q₁·Q₂` contains a representative of the CRT residue
class `x ≡ 0 (mod Q₁)`, `x ≡ -1 (mod Q₂)`.) -/
theorem exists_crt_adjacent {N M Q1 Q2 : ℕ} (hcop : Nat.Coprime Q1 Q2)
    (h1 : 1 ≤ Q1) (h2 : 1 ≤ Q2) (hle : Q1 * Q2 ≤ M - N) :
    ∃ x, N ≤ x ∧ x + 1 ≤ M ∧ Q1 ∣ x ∧ Q2 ∣ (x + 1) := by
  -- By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, there exists an integer $k$ such that $k \equiv 0 \pmod{Q1}$ and $k \equiv -1 \pmod{Q2}$.
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ : ∃ k : ℕ, k ≡ 0 [MOD Q1] ∧ k ≡ -1 [ZMOD Q2] := by
    have := Nat.chineseRemainder hcop 0 ( Q2 - 1 ) ; simp_all +decide [ ← Int.natCast_modEq_iff ] ;
    exact ⟨ this.1, Int.natCast_modEq_iff.mpr this.2.1, Int.ModEq.trans ( Int.natCast_modEq_iff.mpr this.2.2 ) ( Int.modEq_iff_dvd.mpr ⟨ -1, by rw [ Int.ofNat_sub h2 ] ; ring ⟩ ) ⟩;
  refine' ⟨ N + ( ( k % ( Q1 * Q2 ) + Q1 * Q2 - N % ( Q1 * Q2 ) ) % ( Q1 * Q2 ) ), _, _, _, _ ⟩;
  · exact Nat.le_add_right _ _;
  · have := Nat.mod_lt ( k % ( Q1 * Q2 ) + Q1 * Q2 - N % ( Q1 * Q2 ) ) ( by positivity : 0 < Q1 * Q2 );
    omega;
  · rw [ Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero ];
    simp_all +decide [ ← ZMod.val_natCast, Nat.ModEq ];
    rw [ Nat.cast_sub ] <;> norm_num [ hk ];
    · cases Q1 <;> cases Q2 <;> aesop;
    · exact le_add_of_nonneg_of_le ( Nat.zero_le _ ) ( Nat.le_of_lt ( Nat.mod_lt _ ( by positivity ) ) );
  · rw [ ← Int.natCast_dvd_natCast ] ; simp_all +decide [ ← ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd, ← ZMod.intCast_eq_intCast_iff ] ;
    rw [ Nat.cast_sub ] <;> norm_num [ Int.add_emod, Int.sub_emod, Int.mul_emod, hk.2 ];
    · simp_all +decide [ Int.emod_def ];
    · exact le_add_of_nonneg_of_le ( Nat.zero_le _ ) ( Nat.le_of_lt ( Nat.mod_lt _ ( by positivity ) ) )

namespace Gap2CE

variable (ce : Gap2CE)

/-
**Coprime hole-forcing pairing (Target 2).** If `Q₁, Q₂` are coprime positive
hole-forcing moduli with `Q₁·Q₂ ≤ M - N`, then no gap-`≤2` counterexample exists.
-/
theorem coprimeHoleModuli_CRT_pair {Q1 Q2 : ℕ}
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime Q1 Q2) (h1 : 1 ≤ Q1) (h2 : 1 ≤ Q2)
    (hf1 : ce.HoleForcing Q1) (hf2 : ce.HoleForcing Q2)
    (hle : Q1 * Q2 ≤ ce.M - ce.N) : False := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := exists_crt_adjacent hcop h1 h2 hle;
  exact ce.blockerPair_contradiction hx.1 hx.2.1 ( hf1 x ( Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨ hx.1, by linarith ⟩ ) hx.2.2.1 ) ( hf2 ( x + 1 ) ( Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨ by linarith, by linarith ⟩ ) hx.2.2.2 )

/-- Alias of `coprimeHoleModuli_CRT_pair`. -/
theorem coprime_holeForcing_contradiction {Q1 Q2 : ℕ}
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime Q1 Q2) (h1 : 1 ≤ Q1) (h2 : 1 ≤ Q2)
    (hf1 : ce.HoleForcing Q1) (hf2 : ce.HoleForcing Q2)
    (hle : Q1 * Q2 ≤ ce.M - ce.N) : False :=
  ce.coprimeHoleModuli_CRT_pair hcop h1 h2 hf1 hf2 hle

/-- Two distinct primes' ceiling moduli are coprime. -/
theorem coprime_ceilMod {p r : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpr : p ≠ r) :
    Nat.Coprime (ce.ceilMod p) (ce.ceilMod r) :=
  Nat.Coprime.pow _ _ ((Nat.coprime_primes hp hr).mpr hpr)

/-- **Ceiling–CRT contradiction.** For distinct primes `p, r`, `qₚ·q_r ≤ M - N`
is impossible. -/
theorem ceilingCRT_contradiction {p r : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpr : p ≠ r)
    (hle : ce.ceilMod p * ce.ceilMod r ≤ ce.M - ce.N) : False :=
  ce.coprimeHoleModuli_CRT_pair (ce.coprime_ceilMod hp hr hpr)
    (ce.one_le_ceilMod hp) (ce.one_le_ceilMod hr)
    (ce.holeForcing_ceilMod hp) (ce.holeForcing_ceilMod hr) hle

/-- **Ceiling–CRT pairing (Target 3).** For distinct primes `p, r`, `qₚ·q_r > M - N`. -/
theorem ceilingCRT_pairing {p r : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpr : p ≠ r) :
    ce.M - ce.N < ce.ceilMod p * ce.ceilMod r := by
  by_contra h
  exact ce.ceilingCRT_contradiction hp hr hpr (not_lt.mp h)

/-- Alias of `ceilingCRT_pairing`. -/
theorem ceilMod_mul_gt {p r : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpr : p ≠ r) :
    ce.M - ce.N < ce.ceilMod p * ce.ceilMod r :=
  ce.ceilingCRT_pairing hp hr hpr

/-! ## Corollaries (Target 4) -/

/-
**At most one small ceiling modulus (Target 4, Nat form).** For distinct primes
`p, r`, the ceiling moduli cannot both satisfy `qₚ² ≤ M - N`.
-/
theorem atMostOne_small_ceiling {p r : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpr : p ≠ r) :
    ¬ (ce.ceilMod p ^ 2 ≤ ce.M - ce.N ∧ ce.ceilMod r ^ 2 ≤ ce.M - ce.N) := by
  intro h
  have h_prod : (ce.ceilMod p * ce.ceilMod r)^2 ≤ (ce.M - ce.N)^2 := by
    nlinarith;
  exact absurd h_prod ( by nlinarith only [ show 0 < ce.ceilMod p * ce.ceilMod r from mul_pos ( pow_pos hp.pos _ ) ( pow_pos hr.pos _ ), show ce.M - ce.N < ce.ceilMod p * ce.ceilMod r from ceilingCRT_pairing ce hp hr hpr ] )

/-
**At most one small ceiling modulus (√ form).** For distinct primes `p, r`, the
ceiling moduli cannot both be `≤ √(M - N)`.
-/
theorem at_most_one_ceilMod_le_sqrt {p r : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hr : r.Prime)
    (hpr : p ≠ r) :
    ¬ (ce.ceilMod p ≤ Nat.sqrt (ce.M - ce.N) ∧ ce.ceilMod r ≤ Nat.sqrt (ce.M - ce.N)) := by
  intro h
  have h1 : (ce.ceilMod p ^ 2 ≤ ce.M - ce.N) := by
    exact le_trans ( Nat.pow_le_pow_left h.1 2 ) ( Nat.sqrt_le' _ )
  have h2 : (ce.ceilMod r ^ 2 ≤ ce.M - ce.N) := by
    exact le_trans ( Nat.pow_le_pow_left h.2 2 ) ( Nat.sqrt_le' _ )
  exact atMostOne_small_ceiling ce hp hr hpr ⟨h1, h2⟩

/-- **`q₂·q₃ > M - N`.** -/
theorem ceilMod_two_three_gt :
    ce.M - ce.N < ce.ceilMod 2 * ce.ceilMod 3 :=
  ce.ceilingCRT_pairing Nat.prime_two Nat.prime_three (by norm_num)

/-
**`max(q₂, q₃) > √(M - N)`.**
-/
theorem max_ceilMod_two_three_gt_sqrt :
    Nat.sqrt (ce.M - ce.N) < max (ce.ceilMod 2) (ce.ceilMod 3) := by
  have := @at_most_one_ceilMod_le_sqrt ce 2 3 Nat.prime_two Nat.prime_three ( by norm_num );
  grind +extAll

/-! ## The minimal ceiling modulus and the AP-prime reduction (Targets 5–6) -/

/-- `Q` is a ceiling modulus of some prime. -/
def isCeilModOfPrime (Q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ Q = ce.ceilMod p

/-- The **minimal ceiling modulus** `Q = minₚ qₚ`. -/
noncomputable def minCeil : ℕ := sInf {Q | ce.isCeilModOfPrime Q}

/-
The minimal ceiling modulus is itself a ceiling modulus of some prime.
-/
theorem minCeil_isCeilMod : ce.isCeilModOfPrime ce.minCeil := by
  convert Nat.sInf_mem ?_;
  exact ⟨ _, ⟨ 2, Nat.prime_two, rfl ⟩ ⟩

/-
The minimal ceiling modulus is hole-forcing.
-/
theorem minCeil_holeForcing : ce.HoleForcing ce.minCeil := by
  -- By definition of minCeil, obtain the prime p such that minCeil = ceilMod p.
  obtain ⟨p, hp_prime, hp_ceil⟩ : ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ce.minCeil = ce.ceilMod p := by
    convert ce.minCeil_isCeilMod using 1;
  exact hp_ceil ▸ ce.holeForcing_ceilMod hp_prime

/-
**AP-prime kills a hole-forcing modulus (core).** If `M ≥ 8152`, `Q` is
hole-forcing, and `ℓ` is a prime in `[N+1, M-1]` with `Q ∣ ℓ - 1`, then no gap-`≤2`
counterexample exists: `ℓ` is a hole (prime, so not a denominator) and `ℓ-1` is a
`Q`-multiple hole, giving two adjacent holes.
-/
theorem AP_prime_kills_holeForcing {Q ℓ : ℕ} (hM : 8152 ≤ ce.M)
    (hf : ce.HoleForcing Q) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    (hlo : ce.N + 1 ≤ ℓ) (hhi : ℓ ≤ ce.M - 1) (hdvd : Q ∣ (ℓ - 1)) : False := by
  contrapose! hf;
  intro h; have := h ( ℓ - 1 ) ?_ hdvd <;> rcases ℓ with ( _ | _ | ℓ ) <;> simp_all +arith +decide;
  · grind +suggestions;
  · omega

/-- **AP-prime kills a ceiling modulus.** Specialization of `AP_prime_kills_holeForcing`
to `Q = qₚ`. -/
theorem AP_prime_kills_ceiling {p ℓ : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hM : 8152 ≤ ce.M)
    (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hlo : ce.N + 1 ≤ ℓ) (hhi : ℓ ≤ ce.M - 1)
    (hdvd : ce.ceilMod p ∣ (ℓ - 1)) : False :=
  ce.AP_prime_kills_holeForcing hM (ce.holeForcing_ceilMod hp) hℓ hlo hhi hdvd

/-
**AP-prime kills the minimal ceiling (Target 5).** If `M ≥ 8152` and there is a
prime `ℓ ∈ [N+1, M-1]` with `ℓ ≡ 1 (mod Q)` for `Q = minₚ qₚ`, contradiction.
-/
theorem AP_prime_kills_minCeil {ℓ : ℕ} (hM : 8152 ≤ ce.M)
    (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hlo : ce.N + 1 ≤ ℓ) (hhi : ℓ ≤ ce.M - 1)
    (hcong : ℓ ≡ 1 [MOD ce.minCeil]) : False := by
  convert ce.AP_prime_kills_holeForcing hM _ _ _ _ _;
  exact ce.minCeil;
  exact ℓ;
  · grind +suggestions;
  · assumption;
  · linarith;
  · grind;
  · rw [ ← Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd ];
    cases ℓ <;> simp_all +decide [ ← ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff ]

/-- **The analytic AP-prime hypothesis.** `APPrimeInInterval Q N M` asserts the
existence of a prime `ℓ ∈ [N+1, M-1]` with `ℓ ≡ 1 (mod Q)`.  This is *stated*, not
proved; it is the arithmetic-progression input the reduction consumes. -/
def APPrimeInInterval (Q N M : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ N + 1 ≤ ℓ ∧ ℓ ≤ M - 1 ∧ ℓ ≡ 1 [MOD Q]

/-- **Large-Ceiling reduction (Target 6).** Any gap-`≤2` counterexample with
`M ≥ 8152` satisfies both structural conclusions:
* `qₚ·q_r > M - N` for all distinct primes `p, r`;
* no prime `ℓ ∈ [N+1, M-1]` is `≡ 1 (mod Q)` for `Q = minₚ qₚ`. -/
theorem LargeCeilingReduction (hM : 8152 ≤ ce.M) :
    (∀ p r : ℕ, p.Prime → r.Prime → p ≠ r →
      ce.M - ce.N < ce.ceilMod p * ce.ceilMod r) ∧
    (∀ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime → ce.N + 1 ≤ ℓ → ℓ ≤ ce.M - 1 → ¬ (ℓ ≡ 1 [MOD ce.minCeil])) := by
  refine ⟨fun p r hp hr hpr => ce.ceilingCRT_pairing hp hr hpr, ?_⟩
  intro ℓ hℓ hlo hhi hcong
  exact ce.AP_prime_kills_minCeil hM hℓ hlo hhi hcong

/-- **The AP-prime hypothesis refutes a large counterexample (Target 6, optional).**
If the analytic input `APPrimeInInterval Q N M` holds for `Q = minₚ qₚ`, then no
gap-`≤2` counterexample with `M ≥ 8152` exists. -/
theorem no_Gap2CE_of_APPrime (hM : 8152 ≤ ce.M)
    (h : APPrimeInInterval ce.minCeil ce.N ce.M) : False := by
  obtain ⟨ℓ, hℓ, hlo, hhi, hcong⟩ := h
  exact ce.AP_prime_kills_minCeil hM hℓ hlo hhi hcong

end Gap2CE

end Erdos287
