@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=15859 sha256=6b889a36c4e23975dd0283bc76945004c1d12a91c67206a816df02c264e1f837 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/CentredFrontierTriviality.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.BoundedConductorTargetAudit

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — the centred `k = 1` target is qualitatively trivial (§64)

```
UNIFORM ATOM BOUND FOR K_ell           : KERNEL-PROVED
PERIOD-BLOCK BASE INDEPENDENCE         : KERNEL-PROVED
CENTRED WINDOW BOUND (per conductor)   : KERNEL-PROVED
∃ b, CentredBoundedConductorK1Target b : KERNEL-PROVED
```

§62 refuted the bounded-conductor `k = 1` target as formalised, and proposed the
density-centred replacement `CentredBoundedConductorK1Target`.  This module completes the
audit of that replacement: on ordered windows it is **qualitatively trivial** — *some*
budget always works, for a purely structural reason.  The returned kernel is a finite sum of
`ℓ`-periodic kernels with uniformly bounded atoms, so a window sum differs from its density
term only by the incomplete final period, whose contribution is bounded by
`∑_ℓ ℓ·(sup|K_ℓ| + |mean_ℓ|)` independently of `A`, `B` and `z`.

Consequently *no* qualitative boundedness statement about `returnedKernel` can carry analytic
content: the frontier has to be stated **quantitatively** (a specific admissible budget, as
in the ledger targets) and at the level of the physical `X → ∞` source, not for the finite
periodic kernel alone.  This is recorded as a firewall, not as a closure of any owner: the
`k = 1` analytic owner is *not* closed by this module.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §64.1  A uniform bound on the local atoms -/

/-- A uniform (in `s` and `z`) bound for the local kernel `K_ℓ`. -/
def Kbound (ell : ℕ) : ℚ := |cEll ell| * (∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) + 2) + 1)

lemma prod_add_two_pos (ell : ℕ) : (0 : ℚ) < ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) + 2) := by
  refine Finset.prod_pos fun p hp => ?_
  have := (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp).two_le
  have : (2 : ℚ) ≤ (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast this
  linarith

lemma Kbound_nonneg (ell : ℕ) : 0 ≤ Kbound ell := by
  have := prod_add_two_pos ell
  have habs : 0 ≤ |cEll ell| := abs_nonneg _
  have : (0 : ℚ) ≤ ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) + 2) + 1 := by linarith
  exact mul_nonneg habs this

/-- **`abs_Kell_le`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The local kernel is bounded uniformly in the window
variable `s` and in the outer variable `z`. -/
theorem abs_Kell_le {ell : ℕ} (hell : ell ≠ 0) (s z : ℤ) : |Kell ell s z| ≤ Kbound ell := by
  have hmask : |coprimeMask ell (z - s)| ≤ 1 := by
    rw [coprimeMask_eq_indicator hell]
    by_cases h : Int.gcd (ell : ℤ) (z - s) = 1 <;> simp [h]
  have hsub : gcdFactors ell s ⊆ ell.primeFactors := Finset.filter_subset _ _
  have hbrk : |(∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, (2 - (p : ℚ))) - 1|
      ≤ ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) + 2) + 1 := by
    have h1 : |∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, (2 - (p : ℚ))|
        ≤ ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) + 2) := by
      rw [Finset.abs_prod]
      have hstep : ∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, |2 - (p : ℚ)|
          ≤ ∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, ((p : ℚ) + 2) := by
        refine Finset.prod_le_prod (fun p _ => abs_nonneg _) fun p hp => ?_
        have hpp := Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors (hsub hp)
        have : (2 : ℚ) ≤ (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hpp.two_le
        rw [abs_sub_comm, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
        linarith
      refine hstep.trans ?_
      have hone : (1 : ℚ) ≤ ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors \ gcdFactors ell s, ((p : ℚ) + 2) := by
        refine Finset.prod_induction _ (fun x => (1 : ℚ) ≤ x) (fun a b ha hb => by nlinarith)
          le_rfl fun p hp => ?_
        have hpp := Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 hp).1
        have : (2 : ℚ) ≤ (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hpp.two_le
        linarith
      have hnn : (0 : ℚ) ≤ ∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, ((p : ℚ) + 2) := by
        refine Finset.prod_nonneg fun p hp => ?_
        have hpp := Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors (hsub hp)
        have : (2 : ℚ) ≤ (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hpp.two_le
        linarith
      have hsd := Finset.prod_sdiff (f := fun p : ℕ => ((p : ℚ) + 2)) hsub
      nlinarith
    calc |(∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, (2 - (p : ℚ))) - 1|
        ≤ |∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, (2 - (p : ℚ))| + |(1 : ℚ)| := abs_sub _ _
      _ ≤ ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) + 2) + 1 := by
          have : |(1 : ℚ)| = 1 := abs_one
          linarith
  rw [Kell, Kbound, abs_mul, abs_mul]
  have h0 : 0 ≤ |cEll ell| := abs_nonneg _
  have hstep : |cEll ell| * |coprimeMask ell (z - s)| ≤ |cEll ell| * 1 :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hmask h0
  have hbrk0 : 0 ≤ |(∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, (2 - (p : ℚ))) - 1| := abs_nonneg _
  calc |cEll ell| * |coprimeMask ell (z - s)|
          * |(∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, (2 - (p : ℚ))) - 1|
      ≤ (|cEll ell| * 1) * |(∏ p ∈ gcdFactors ell s, (2 - (p : ℚ))) - 1| :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hstep hbrk0
    _ ≤ |cEll ell| * (∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) + 2) + 1) := by
        rw [mul_one]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbrk h0

/-! ## §64.2  Period blocks do not depend on the base point -/

/-- Splitting an integer window at an interior point. -/
lemma sum_Ico_split {f : ℤ → ℚ} {A C B : ℤ} (hAC : A ≤ C) (hCB : C ≤ B) :
    ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A C, f s + ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, f s = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, f s := by
  rw [← Finset.sum_union (Finset.Ico_disjoint_Ico_consecutive A C B),
    Finset.Ico_union_Ico_eq_Ico hAC hCB]

/-- Shifting a one-period window by one step does not change its sum. -/
lemma periodBlock_shift_one {f : ℤ → ℚ} {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hper : ∀ s, f (s + m) = f s)
    (A : ℤ) :
    ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (A + 1) (A + 1 + (m : ℤ)), f s = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A (A + (m : ℤ)), f s := by
  have hm' : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (m : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hm
  have h1 : Finset.Ico A (A + (m : ℤ)) = insert A (Finset.Ico (A + 1) (A + (m : ℤ))) := by
    ext s; simp only [Finset.mem_Ico, Finset.mem_insert]; omega
  have h2 : Finset.Ico (A + 1) (A + 1 + (m : ℤ))
      = insert (A + (m : ℤ)) (Finset.Ico (A + 1) (A + (m : ℤ))) := by
    ext s; simp only [Finset.mem_Ico, Finset.mem_insert]; omega
  have hn1 : A ∉ Finset.Ico (A + 1) (A + (m : ℤ)) := by simp
  have hn2 : A + (m : ℤ) ∉ Finset.Ico (A + 1) (A + (m : ℤ)) := by simp
  rw [h1, h2, Finset.sum_insert hn1, Finset.sum_insert hn2, hper A]

/-- **`periodBlock_base_independent`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A complete period block has the
same sum wherever it starts. -/
theorem periodBlock_base_independent {f : ℤ → ℚ} {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m)
    (hper : ∀ s, f (s + m) = f s) (A : ℤ) :
    ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A (A + (m : ℤ)), f s = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (m : ℤ), f s := by
  induction A using Int.induction_on with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have := periodBlock_shift_one hm hper (n : ℤ)
      rw [show ((n : ℤ) + 1) = ((n : ℤ) + 1) from rfl] at this
      rw [show ((n : ℤ) + 1 + (m : ℤ)) = ((n : ℤ) + 1 + (m : ℤ)) from rfl] at this
      rw [this, ih]
  | pred n ih =>
      have := periodBlock_shift_one hm hper (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
      have heq : (-(n : ℤ) - 1 + 1) = -(n : ℤ) := by ring
      rw [heq] at this
      rw [← this, ih]

/-- **`sum_blocks`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A window consisting of `q` complete periods. -/
theorem sum_blocks {f : ℤ → ℚ} {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hper : ∀ s, f (s + m) = f s)
    (A : ℤ) (q : ℕ) :
    ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A (A + (m : ℤ) * (q : ℤ)), f s
      = (q : ℚ) * ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (m : ℤ), f s := by
  induction q with
  | zero => simp
  | succ q ih =>
      have hsplit : ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A (A + (m : ℤ) * (q : ℤ)), f s
            + ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (A + (m : ℤ) * (q : ℤ))
                (A + (m : ℤ) * ((q : ℤ) + 1)), f s
          = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A (A + (m : ℤ) * ((q : ℤ) + 1)), f s := by
        refine sum_Ico_split ?_ ?_ <;>
          nlinarith [Int.natCast_nonneg m, Int.natCast_nonneg q,
            (by exact_mod_cast hm : (1:ℤ) ≤ (m:ℤ))]
      have hblock : ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (A + (m : ℤ) * (q : ℤ))
            (A + (m : ℤ) * ((q : ℤ) + 1)), f s
          = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) (m : ℤ), f s := by
        have hrw : A + (m : ℤ) * ((q : ℤ) + 1) = (A + (m : ℤ) * (q : ℤ)) + (m : ℤ) := by ring
        rw [hrw, periodBlock_base_independent hm hper]
      push_cast
      rw [← hsplit, hblock, ih]
      ring

/-! ## §64.3  The incomplete final period is uniformly bounded -/

lemma abs_sum_Ico_le {f : ℤ → ℚ} {C B : ℤ} {c : ℚ} (hCB : C ≤ B) (hc : ∀ s, |f s| ≤ c) :
    |∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, f s| ≤ ((B - C : ℤ) : ℚ) * c := by
  have hcard : ((Finset.Ico C B).card : ℤ) = B - C := by
    rw [Int.card_Ico]; omega
  have h1 : |∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, f s| ≤ ∑ _s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, c :=
    (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans (Finset.sum_le_sum fun s _ => hc s)
  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul] at h1
  have hcast : ((Finset.Ico C B).card : ℚ) = ((B - C : ℤ) : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hcard
  rwa [hcast] at h1

/-- **`perSum_eq_mul_perMean`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`. -/
theorem perSum_eq_mul_perMean {ell : ℕ} (hell : 0 < ell) (z : ℤ) :
    perSum ell z = (ell : ℚ) * perMean ell z := by
  have hne : (ell : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  rw [perMean, mul_div_cancel₀ _ hne]

/-- **`windowSum_centred_bound`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For each internal conductor, the
window sum differs from its density term by at most one incomplete period. -/
theorem windowSum_centred_bound {ell : ℕ} (hellpos : 0 < ell) (A B z : ℤ) (hAB : A ≤ B) :
    |∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, Kell ell s z - ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) * perMean ell z|
      ≤ (ell : ℚ) * (Kbound ell + |perMean ell z|) := by
  have hper : ∀ s : ℤ, Kell ell (s + ell) z = Kell ell s z := fun s => Kell_periodic ell s z
  set L : ℕ := (B - A).toNat with hL
  set q : ℕ := L / ell with hq
  set r : ℕ := L % ell with hr
  have hLqr : L = ell * q + r := (Nat.div_add_mod L ell).symm
  have hrlt : r < ell := Nat.mod_lt _ hellpos
  have hLz : (L : ℤ) = B - A := by omega
  have hz : (L : ℤ) = (ell : ℤ) * (q : ℤ) + (r : ℤ) := by
    exact_mod_cast congrArg (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℤ)) hLqr
  set C : ℤ := A + (ell : ℤ) * (q : ℤ) with hC
  have hAC : A ≤ C := by
    have : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (ell : ℤ) * (q : ℤ) := by positivity
    omega
  have hCB : C ≤ B := by omega
  have hsplit : ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A C, Kell ell s z + ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, Kell ell s z
      = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, Kell ell s z :=
    sum_Ico_split hAC hCB
  have hblocks : ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A C, Kell ell s z = (q : ℚ) * ((ell : ℚ) * perMean ell z) := by
    rw [hC, sum_blocks hellpos hper A q, sum_Ico_eq_sum_range (fun s : ℤ => Kell ell s z) ell]
    have hps : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range ell, Kell ell (i : ℤ) z = perSum ell z := rfl
    rw [hps, perSum_eq_mul_perMean hellpos]
  have hrem : |∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, Kell ell s z| ≤ ((B - C : ℤ) : ℚ) * Kbound ell :=
    abs_sum_Ico_le hCB (fun s => abs_Kell_le (by omega) s z)
  have hBC : ((B - C : ℤ) : ℚ) = (r : ℚ) := by
    have : B - C = (r : ℤ) := by omega
    rw [this]; norm_num
  have hBA : ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) = (ell : ℚ) * (q : ℚ) + (r : ℚ) := by
    have hBA' : B - A = (ell : ℤ) * (q : ℤ) + (r : ℤ) := by omega
    rw [hBA']; push_cast; ring
  have hdiff : ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, Kell ell s z - ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) * perMean ell z
      = ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, Kell ell s z - (r : ℚ) * perMean ell z := by
    rw [← hsplit, hblocks, hBA]
    ring
  rw [hBC] at hrem
  rw [hdiff]
  have hrle : (r : ℚ) ≤ (ell : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hrlt.le
  have hr0 : (0 : ℚ) ≤ (r : ℚ) := by positivity
  have hK0 : 0 ≤ Kbound ell := Kbound_nonneg ell
  have hm0 : (0 : ℚ) ≤ |perMean ell z| := abs_nonneg _
  have habs2 : |(r : ℚ) * perMean ell z| = (r : ℚ) * |perMean ell z| := by
    rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg hr0]
  have hstep : |∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico C B, Kell ell s z - (r : ℚ) * perMean ell z|
      ≤ (r : ℚ) * Kbound ell + (r : ℚ) * |perMean ell z| := by
    refine (abs_sub _ _).trans ?_
    linarith [hrem, habs2.le, habs2.ge]
  have hfin : (r : ℚ) * Kbound ell + (r : ℚ) * |perMean ell z|
      ≤ (ell : ℚ) * (Kbound ell + |perMean ell z|) := by nlinarith
  linarith

/-! ## §64.4  Qualitative triviality of the centred target -/

/-- The explicit qualitative budget. -/
def centredBudget : ℚ := ∑ ell ∈ conductorRange, (ell : ℚ) * (Kbound ell + Kbound ell)

/-- The `z`-uniform bound on the complete-period mean. -/
lemma abs_perMean_le {ell : ℕ} (hell : 0 < ell) (z : ℤ) : |perMean ell z| ≤ Kbound ell := by
  have hne : (0 : ℚ) < (ell : ℚ) := by positivity
  have h1 : |perSum ell z| ≤ (ell : ℚ) * Kbound ell := by
    refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans ?_
    have : ∑ s ∈ Finset.range ell, |Kell ell (s : ℤ) z| ≤ ∑ _s ∈ Finset.range ell, Kbound ell :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum fun s _ => abs_Kell_le (by omega) _ _
    simpa [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_range, nsmul_eq_mul] using this
  rw [perMean, abs_div, abs_of_nonneg hne.le, div_le_iff₀ hne]
  linarith [h1]

/-- **`centred_target_satisfiable`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The density-centred `k = 1` target is
satisfied by an explicit budget: *qualitative* boundedness of the returned finite-conductor
kernel carries no analytic content, because the kernel is a finite sum of periodic kernels
with uniformly bounded atoms.  A *quantitative* budget (as demanded by the ledger) is a
different, still open, question. -/
theorem centred_target_satisfiable : CentredBoundedConductorK1Target centredBudget := by
  intro A B z hAB
  rw [centredBudget]
  have hterm : ∀ ell ∈ conductorRange,
      |∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, Kell ell s z - ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) * perMean ell z|
        ≤ (ell : ℚ) * (Kbound ell + Kbound ell) := by
    intro ell hell
    rw [conductorRange, Finset.mem_Icc] at hell
    have hpos : 0 < ell := by omega
    refine (windowSum_centred_bound hpos A B z hAB).trans ?_
    have hle := abs_perMean_le hpos z
    have : (0 : ℚ) ≤ (ell : ℚ) := by positivity
    nlinarith
  have hrw : returnedKernel A B z - ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) * meanSumAt z
      = ∑ ell ∈ conductorRange,
          (∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, Kell ell s z - ((B - A : ℤ) : ℚ) * perMean ell z) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, ← meanSumAt, returnedKernel,
      show Finset.Icc 1001 5000 = conductorRange from rfl]
    refine congrArg₂ _ (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ell hell => ?_) rfl
    rw [conductorRange, Finset.mem_Icc] at hell
    exact (Qell_compiler (by omega : 0 < ell) A B z).symm
  rw [hrw]
  refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans (Finset.sum_le_sum hterm)

/-- **`centred_target_exists_budget`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`. -/
theorem centred_target_exists_budget : ∃ b : ℚ, CentredBoundedConductorK1Target b :=
  ⟨centredBudget, centred_target_satisfiable⟩

/-- **`qualitative_boundedness_has_no_analytic_content`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` firewall.  The
uncentred target is false for every budget while the centred target holds for some budget:
neither statement is an analytic theorem about the source.  The `k = 1` owner is therefore
**not** closed by this module; what remains is the *quantitative* budget question. -/
theorem qualitative_boundedness_has_no_analytic_content :
    (∀ b : ℚ, ¬ BoundedConductorK1Target b) ∧ (∃ b : ℚ, CentredBoundedConductorK1Target b) :=
  ⟨boundedConductorK1Target_unsatisfiable, centred_target_exists_budget⟩

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=5263 sha256=059320d70d89ff5561b10e27268a9d83ed8e9839d527411a15097c8c19d04d40 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Chain.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Blocker

/-!
# Erdős Problem #287 — range-covering blocker pairs and finite chain certificates

Target 6.  A single blocker pair at `x` (with excluded prime powers dividing `x` and
`x+1`) already refutes every `Gap2CE` whose maximum `M` lies in the range
`[x+2, ⌊e·x⌋]` (`Gap2CE.blockerPair_covers_range`): the analytic lower bound
`e·(N-1) < M ≤ e·x` forces `N ≤ x`, so `x, x+1 ∈ [N, M]`.

We then bundle a list of such pairs into a finite **chain certificate** whose covered
`M`-ranges overlap to cover a whole interval `[lo, hi]` (`BlockerChain`), and prove that
any such certificate refutes every `Gap2CE` with `M ∈ [lo, hi]` (`BlockerChain.refutes`).
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287

/-
`ExcludedPP` is monotone downward in the window bound `M`.
-/
theorem ExcludedPP.mono_M {M M' q : ℕ} (h : ExcludedPP M q) (hM : M' ≤ M) :
    ExcludedPP M' q := by
  obtain ⟨ p, e, hp, he, rfl, hpC ⟩ := h;
  exact ⟨ p, e, hp, he, rfl, lt_of_le_of_lt ( C_mono ( Nat.div_le_div_right hM ) ) hpC ⟩

namespace Gap2CE

variable (ce : Gap2CE)

/-
**Blocker pair covers a range.**  A blocker pair at `x` refutes every `Gap2CE`
whose maximum satisfies `x + 2 ≤ M` and `(M : ℝ) ≤ e · x` (i.e. `M ≤ ⌊e·x⌋`).
-/
theorem blockerPair_covers_range {x q₁ q₂ : ℕ}
    (hMlow : x + 2 ≤ ce.M)
    (hMhigh : (ce.M : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp 1 * x)
    (hq1 : ExcludedPP ce.M q₁) (hq2 : ExcludedPP ce.M q₂)
    (hd1 : q₁ ∣ x) (hd2 : q₂ ∣ x + 1) : False := by
  have := @Gap2CE.excludedPP_blockerPair;
  contrapose! this;
  refine' ⟨ ce, x, q₁, q₂, _, _, hq1, hq2, hd1, hd2, trivial ⟩;
  · exact Nat.le_of_lt_succ ( by rw [ ← @Nat.cast_lt ℝ ] ; push_cast; nlinarith [ Real.add_one_le_exp 1, show ( ce.M : ℝ ) ≥ x + 2 by norm_cast, Gap2CE.exp_lower ce ] );
  · linarith

end Gap2CE

/-! ## Finite chain certificates -/

/-- A single certified blocker pair, together with the top `Mmax` of the `M`-range it
covers.  `hrange` guarantees `Mmax ≤ ⌊e·x⌋`, so the pair refutes every `Gap2CE` with
`x + 2 ≤ M ≤ Mmax`. -/
structure ChainLink where
  /-- The blocking integer. -/
  x : ℕ
  /-- Top of the covered `M`-range. -/
  Mmax : ℕ
  /-- Prime power dividing `x`. -/
  q₁ : ℕ
  /-- Prime power dividing `x+1`. -/
  q₂ : ℕ
  /-- `q₁ ∣ x`. -/
  hd1 : q₁ ∣ x
  /-- `q₂ ∣ x+1`. -/
  hd2 : q₂ ∣ x + 1
  /-- `q₁` is excluded on `[1, Mmax]`. -/
  hexc1 : ExcludedPP Mmax q₁
  /-- `q₂` is excluded on `[1, Mmax]`. -/
  hexc2 : ExcludedPP Mmax q₂
  /-- `Mmax ≤ ⌊e·x⌋`. -/
  hrange : (Mmax : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp 1 * x

/-- The `M`-range covered by a single link: `[x+2, Mmax]`. -/
def ChainLink.covers (L : ChainLink) (M : ℕ) : Prop := L.x + 2 ≤ M ∧ M ≤ L.Mmax

/-
A single link refutes every `Gap2CE` whose maximum it covers.
-/
theorem ChainLink.refutes (L : ChainLink) (ce : Gap2CE) (h : L.covers ce.M) : False := by
  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := h;
  apply Gap2CE.blockerPair_covers_range;
  exact hlo;
  exact le_trans ( Nat.cast_le.mpr hhi ) L.hrange;
  exact ExcludedPP.mono_M L.hexc1 hhi;
  exact ExcludedPP.mono_M L.hexc2 hhi;
  · exact L.hd1;
  · exact L.hd2

/-- A list of links covers `M` if some member does. -/
def Covers (links : List ChainLink) (M : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ L ∈ links, L.covers M

/-
If a list of links covers `ce.M`, it refutes the `Gap2CE`.
-/
theorem covers_refutes (links : List ChainLink) (ce : Gap2CE)
    (h : Covers links ce.M) : False := by
  exact h.elim fun L hL => L.refutes ce hL.2

/-- `chainFrom lo links hi`: the links, read in order, cover `[lo, hi]` with no gaps —
each link starts no later than the running lower bound, and its `Mmax + 1` becomes the
next lower bound. -/
def chainFrom (lo : ℕ) : List ChainLink → ℕ → Prop
  | [], hi => hi < lo
  | L :: rest, hi => L.x + 2 ≤ lo ∧ chainFrom (L.Mmax + 1) rest hi

/-
A chained list covers every point of `[lo, hi]`.
-/
theorem chainFrom_covers :
    ∀ (links : List ChainLink) (lo hi M : ℕ),
      chainFrom lo links hi → lo ≤ M → M ≤ hi → Covers links M := by
  intro links lo hi M h_chain hlo hhi
  induction' links with L rest ih generalizing lo hi;
  · grind +locals;
  · cases h_chain;
    by_cases hM : M ≤ L.Mmax;
    · exact ⟨ L, List.mem_cons_self, ⟨ by linarith, hM ⟩ ⟩;
    · exact Exists.elim ( ih _ _ ‹_› ( by linarith ) ( by linarith ) ) fun x hx => ⟨ x, List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hx.1, hx.2 ⟩

/-- A finite chain certificate: a list of blocker links whose covered ranges chain to
cover the whole interval `[lo, hi]`. -/
structure BlockerChain where
  /-- The certified blocker links, in increasing order. -/
  links : List ChainLink
  /-- Lower endpoint of the covered interval. -/
  lo : ℕ
  /-- Upper endpoint of the covered interval. -/
  hi : ℕ
  /-- The links chain to cover `[lo, hi]`. -/
  chain : chainFrom lo links hi

/-
**Any valid chain certificate refutes every `Gap2CE` with `M ∈ [lo, hi]`.**
-/
theorem BlockerChain.refutes (BC : BlockerChain) (ce : Gap2CE)
    (hlo : BC.lo ≤ ce.M) (hhi : ce.M ≤ BC.hi) : False := by
  convert covers_refutes BC.links ce ( chainFrom_covers BC.links BC.lo BC.hi ce.M BC.chain hlo hhi ) using 1

end Erdos287
@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=12766 sha256=5cc299014c11548f128633771a38191311d79a68599518de0082a7ea8b83aa31 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/CharacterGram3221.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.HighConductorVariance3221

/-!
# V19, Phase H — the character expansion socket and the five-box factorisation

`3221-CHARACTER-ORTHOGONALITY-PROJECTION45 : PROVED_FINITE`
`3221-CHARACTER-GRAM-EXPANSION45 : PROVED_FINITE`
`3221-FIVEBOX-CHARACTER-FACTORISATION45 : PROVED_FINITE`

Dirichlet-character definitions, the conductor, and the full orthogonality relation are all
available, so the low/high conductor projection is **defined literally** and the projection
equality is **proved**, not postulated: no free `Prop` placeholder and no invented character
theory appear anywhere.

## Contents

* `cHat` — the finite character transform `ĉ_q(χ) = ∑_w c(w) χ(w)`.
* `totient_mul_residueSum_eq_sum_char` — the exact orthogonality expansion
  `φ(q) · C_q(a) = ∑_χ χ(a⁻¹) ĉ_q(χ)` for a unit residue `a`.
* `lowSet`, `highSet`, `cLow`, `cHigh` — the literal conductor projections at cutoff `D`,
  and `residueSum_eq_cLow_add_cHigh`, the exact splitting `C_q = C_q^{≤D} + C_q^{>D}`.
* `gram_expansion` — the exact Gram identity for a finite family.
* `highResidue_energy_gram` — the exact `m`-Gram expansion of the high-conductor square,
  and `inverseSampled_highResidue_gram`, its substitution at the inverse sampling point
  `a = −s (2m)⁻¹`.
* `cHat_fiveBox_factorisation`, `cHat_twoBox_factorisation` — the exact factorisation of
  the character transform over a labelled product box (`1+2+2+2`, and the two-prime
  convolutions inside a pair block).

**No character-sum bound is proved, assumed, or implied.**  Every statement here is a
finite algebraic identity.  Erdős #287 remains OPEN; Balanced7 remains OPEN.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Finset
open scoped BigOperators
open scoped Classical

namespace Erdos287
namespace CharGram3221

/-! ## §15a. The finite character transform and orthogonality -/

/-- The finite character transform `ĉ_q(χ) = ∑_{w ∈ Wbox} c(w) χ(w)`. -/
noncomputable def cHat (q : ℕ) (Wbox : Finset ℤ) (c : ℤ → ℂ)
    (chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) : ℂ :=
  ∑ w ∈ Wbox, c w * chi ((w : ZMod q))

/-- **The exact orthogonality expansion.**  `PROVED_FINITE`.

For a unit residue `a` modulo `q`,

`φ(q) · C_q(a) = ∑_{χ mod q} χ(a⁻¹) ĉ_q(χ)`. -/
theorem totient_mul_residueSum_eq_sum_char {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (Wbox : Finset ℤ) (c : ℤ → ℂ)
    {a : ZMod q} (ha : IsUnit a) :
    (q.totient : ℂ) * Erdos287.HighCond3221.residueSum q Wbox c a
      = ∑ chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, chi a⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi := by
  have h1 : ∑ chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, chi a⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi
      = ∑ w ∈ Wbox, c w * ∑ chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, chi a⁻¹ * chi ((w : ZMod q)) := by
    simp only [cHat, Finset.mul_sum]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun w _ =>
      Finset.sum_congr rfl fun chi _ => by ring
  rw [h1]
  simp only [DirichletCharacter.sum_char_inv_mul_char_eq ℂ ha]
  rw [Erdos287.HighCond3221.residueSum, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_filter]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun w _ => ?_
  by_cases h : ((w : ZMod q)) = a
  · simp [h, mul_comm]
  · have h' : ¬ (a = ((w : ZMod q))) := fun hc => h hc.symm
    simp [h, h']

/-! ## §15b. The literal low/high conductor projection -/

/-- The characters of conductor at most `D`. -/
noncomputable def lowSet (q D : ℕ) : Finset (DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun chi => chi.conductor ≤ D)

/-- The characters of conductor above `D`. -/
noncomputable def highSet (q D : ℕ) : Finset (DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun chi => ¬ chi.conductor ≤ D)

/-- The low-conductor projection `C_q^{≤D}`. -/
noncomputable def cLow (q D : ℕ) (Wbox : Finset ℤ) (c : ℤ → ℂ) (a : ZMod q) : ℂ :=
  (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ chi ∈ lowSet q D, chi a⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi

/-- The high-conductor projection `C_q^{>D}`. -/
noncomputable def cHigh (q D : ℕ) (Wbox : Finset ℤ) (c : ℤ → ℂ) (a : ZMod q) : ℂ :=
  (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ chi ∈ highSet q D, chi a⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi

/-- **The literal projection equality.**  `PROVED_FINITE`.

`C_q(a) = C_q^{≤D}(a) + C_q^{>D}(a)` for every unit residue `a`. -/
theorem residueSum_eq_cLow_add_cHigh {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (D : ℕ) (Wbox : Finset ℤ)
    (c : ℤ → ℂ) {a : ZMod q} (ha : IsUnit a) :
    Erdos287.HighCond3221.residueSum q Wbox c a
      = cLow q D Wbox c a + cHigh q D Wbox c a := by
  have htot : (q.totient : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
    have : 0 < q.totient := Nat.totient_pos.mpr (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (NeZero.ne q))
    exact_mod_cast this.ne'
  have hsplit :
      (∑ chi ∈ lowSet q D, chi a⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi)
        + (∑ chi ∈ highSet q D, chi a⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi)
      = ∑ chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, chi a⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi := by
    rw [lowSet, highSet]
    exact Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not _ _ _
  rw [cLow, cHigh, ← mul_add, hsplit, ← totient_mul_residueSum_eq_sum_char Wbox c ha,
    ← mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel₀ htot, one_mul]

/-! ## §15c. The exact Gram expansion -/

/-- **The exact Gram identity for a finite family.**  `PROVED_ALGEBRAIC`. -/
theorem gram_expansion {ι κ : Type*} (Ms : Finset ι) (T : Finset κ) (F : κ → ι → ℂ) :
    ∑ m ∈ Ms, (∑ chi ∈ T, F chi m) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (∑ psi ∈ T, F psi m)
      = ∑ chi ∈ T, ∑ psi ∈ T, ∑ m ∈ Ms, F chi m * (starRingEnd ℂ) (F psi m) := by
  have hstep : ∀ m ∈ Ms, (∑ chi ∈ T, F chi m) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (∑ psi ∈ T, F psi m)
      = ∑ chi ∈ T, ∑ psi ∈ T, F chi m * (starRingEnd ℂ) (F psi m) := by
    intro m _
    rw [map_sum, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hstep, Finset.sum_comm]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun chi _ => Finset.sum_comm

/-- The `m`-Gram factor `G_M(χ, ψ) = ∑_m χ(a_m⁻¹) conj(ψ(a_m⁻¹))`. -/
noncomputable def GM (q : ℕ) (Ms : Finset ℕ) (pt : ℕ → ZMod q)
    (chi psi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) : ℂ :=
  ∑ m ∈ Ms, chi (pt m)⁻¹ * (starRingEnd ℂ) (psi (pt m)⁻¹)

/-- **`highResidue_energy_gram`.**  `PROVED_FINITE`.

The exact `m`-Gram expansion of the high-conductor square:

`∑_m |C_q^{>D}(a_m)|² = φ(q)^{-2} ∑_{χ,ψ high} ĉ(χ) conj(ĉ(ψ)) G_M(χ, ψ)`.

**This is an identity, not an estimate.** -/
theorem highResidue_energy_gram {q : ℕ} (D : ℕ) (Wbox : Finset ℤ) (c : ℤ → ℂ)
    (Ms : Finset ℕ) (pt : ℕ → ZMod q) :
    ∑ m ∈ Ms, cHigh q D Wbox c (pt m) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (cHigh q D Wbox c (pt m))
      = (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∑ chi ∈ highSet q D, ∑ psi ∈ highSet q D,
          cHat q Wbox c chi * (starRingEnd ℂ) (cHat q Wbox c psi) * GM q Ms pt chi psi := by
  have hct : (starRingEnd ℂ) ((q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹) = (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ := by
    rw [map_inv₀]; norm_num
  have hstep : ∀ m ∈ Ms,
      cHigh q D Wbox c (pt m) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (cHigh q D Wbox c (pt m))
        = (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ ^ 2 *
            ((∑ chi ∈ highSet q D, chi (pt m)⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi) *
              (starRingEnd ℂ) (∑ psi ∈ highSet q D, psi (pt m)⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c psi)) := by
    intro m _
    rw [cHigh, map_mul, hct]
    ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hstep, ← Finset.mul_sum,
    gram_expansion Ms (highSet q D) (fun chi m => chi (pt m)⁻¹ * cHat q Wbox c chi)]
  congr 1
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun chi _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun psi _ => ?_
  rw [GM, Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun m _ => ?_
  rw [map_mul]
  ring

/-- **The inverse-sampled substitution.**  `PROVED_FINITE`.

The same identity with `a = −s (2m)⁻¹`, i.e. at the inverse sampling point of the
high-conductor variance socket. -/
theorem inverseSampled_highResidue_gram
    (Dat : Erdos287.HighCond3221.InverseSampledHighCond3221Data) {q : ℕ} (D : ℕ)
    (Wbox : Finset ℤ) (c : ℤ → ℂ) :
    ∑ m ∈ Dat.Mbox, cHigh q D Wbox c (Dat.samplePoint q m) *
        (starRingEnd ℂ) (cHigh q D Wbox c (Dat.samplePoint q m))
      = (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∑ chi ∈ highSet q D, ∑ psi ∈ highSet q D,
          cHat q Wbox c chi * (starRingEnd ℂ) (cHat q Wbox c psi) *
            GM q Dat.Mbox (fun m => Dat.samplePoint q m) chi psi :=
  highResidue_energy_gram D Wbox c Dat.Mbox (fun m => Dat.samplePoint q m)

/-! ## §16. The five-box character factorisation

The labelled `1+2+2+2` source is supported on a product box, and a Dirichlet character is
multiplicative, so its character transform factorises **exactly**.  No bound is claimed for
any of the five factors. -/

/-- A four-fold product of finite sums expands exactly into the four-fold nested sum. -/
theorem sum_mul_sum4 {i1 i2 i3 i4 : Type*} (s1 : Finset i1) (s2 : Finset i2)
    (s3 : Finset i3) (s4 : Finset i4) (f1 : i1 → ℂ) (f2 : i2 → ℂ) (f3 : i3 → ℂ)
    (f4 : i4 → ℂ) :
    (∑ i ∈ s1, f1 i) * (∑ j ∈ s2, f2 j) * (∑ k ∈ s3, f3 k) * (∑ l ∈ s4, f4 l)
      = ∑ i ∈ s1, ∑ j ∈ s2, ∑ k ∈ s3, ∑ l ∈ s4, f1 i * f2 j * f3 k * f4 l := by
  have h1 : (∑ k ∈ s3, f3 k) * (∑ l ∈ s4, f4 l) = ∑ k ∈ s3, ∑ l ∈ s4, f3 k * f4 l :=
    Finset.sum_mul_sum _ _ _ _
  have h2 : (∑ j ∈ s2, f2 j) * (∑ k ∈ s3, ∑ l ∈ s4, f3 k * f4 l)
      = ∑ j ∈ s2, ∑ k ∈ s3, ∑ l ∈ s4, f2 j * (f3 k * f4 l) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => Finset.mul_sum _ _ _
  have h3 : (∑ i ∈ s1, f1 i) * (∑ j ∈ s2, ∑ k ∈ s3, ∑ l ∈ s4, f2 j * (f3 k * f4 l))
      = ∑ i ∈ s1, ∑ j ∈ s2, ∑ k ∈ s3, ∑ l ∈ s4, f1 i * (f2 j * (f3 k * f4 l)) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => Finset.mul_sum _ _ _
  rw [show (∑ i ∈ s1, f1 i) * (∑ j ∈ s2, f2 j) * (∑ k ∈ s3, f3 k) * (∑ l ∈ s4, f4 l)
      = (∑ i ∈ s1, f1 i) * ((∑ j ∈ s2, f2 j) * ((∑ k ∈ s3, f3 k) * (∑ l ∈ s4, f4 l))) by ring,
    h1, h2, h3]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ =>
    Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun l _ => by ring

/-- **`cHat_twoBox_factorisation`.**  `PROVED_FINITE`.

The two-prime convolution inside a pair block factorises exactly under the character
transform. -/
theorem cHat_twoBox_factorisation {q : ℕ} (chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (P1 P2 : Finset ℕ) (om1 om2 : ℕ → ℂ) :
    ∑ p ∈ P1, ∑ r ∈ P2, om1 p * om2 r * chi ((p * r : ℕ) : ZMod q)
      = (∑ p ∈ P1, om1 p * chi ((p : ℕ) : ZMod q))
        * (∑ r ∈ P2, om2 r * chi ((r : ℕ) : ZMod q)) := by
  have hmul : ∀ p r : ℕ, chi ((p * r : ℕ) : ZMod q)
      = chi ((p : ℕ) : ZMod q) * chi ((r : ℕ) : ZMod q) := by
    intro p r
    push_cast
    rw [map_mul]
  calc ∑ p ∈ P1, ∑ r ∈ P2, om1 p * om2 r * chi ((p * r : ℕ) : ZMod q)
      = ∑ p ∈ P1, (om1 p * chi ((p : ℕ) : ZMod q)) *
          ∑ r ∈ P2, om2 r * chi ((r : ℕ) : ZMod q) := by
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => ?_
        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => ?_
        rw [hmul]; ring
    _ = (∑ p ∈ P1, om1 p * chi ((p : ℕ) : ZMod q))
          * (∑ r ∈ P2, om2 r * chi ((r : ℕ) : ZMod q)) := by
        rw [← Finset.sum_mul]

/-- **`cHat_fiveBox_factorisation`.**  `PROVED_FINITE`.

The labelled `1+2+2+2` product box: `e · a · b · c` with independent coefficients.  The
character transform factorises into the four block transforms exactly. -/
theorem cHat_fiveBox_factorisation {q : ℕ} (chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (Ebox Abox Bbox Cbox : Finset ℕ) (eta alpha beta gamma : ℕ → ℂ) :
    ∑ e ∈ Ebox, ∑ a ∈ Abox, ∑ b ∈ Bbox, ∑ cc ∈ Cbox,
        eta e * alpha a * beta b * gamma cc * chi ((e * a * b * cc : ℕ) : ZMod q)
      = (∑ e ∈ Ebox, eta e * chi ((e : ℕ) : ZMod q))
        * (∑ a ∈ Abox, alpha a * chi ((a : ℕ) : ZMod q))
        * (∑ b ∈ Bbox, beta b * chi ((b : ℕ) : ZMod q))
        * (∑ cc ∈ Cbox, gamma cc * chi ((cc : ℕ) : ZMod q)) := by
  have hmul : ∀ e a b cc : ℕ, chi ((e * a * b * cc : ℕ) : ZMod q)
      = chi ((e : ℕ) : ZMod q) * chi ((a : ℕ) : ZMod q) * chi ((b : ℕ) : ZMod q)
        * chi ((cc : ℕ) : ZMod q) := by
    intro e a b cc
    push_cast
    rw [map_mul, map_mul, map_mul]
  rw [sum_mul_sum4]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun e _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ =>
    Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun cc _ => by
      rw [hmul]; ring

end CharGram3221
end Erdos287

@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=7134 sha256=22f3f2c02cda8c5572a8c00fbf620b89225242a84030dea40e2d229dd28ce950 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/ChartEquivalence.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.LambdaWeights
import RequestProject.Erdos287.AllQResummation

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — chart-equivalence and retired-theorem firewalls (§29)

```
CHART EQUIVALENCE       : KERNEL-PROVED (source typing)
DOUBLE-CHARGE FIREWALL  : KERNEL-PROVED
UNWEIGHTED CJOINT 0.09  : RETIRED / FIREWALLED
```

The λ-weighted covariance chart and the all-`q` resummation chart are two *representations*
of one and the same physical medium-`k` long-fibre source once the fibre modulus, the medium
cutoff `K0`, the replayed edge cutoff and the lane agree.  This is bookkeeping, not analysis:
nothing here bounds either chart.  Its content is the prohibition
`chart_double_charge_illegal`: a ledger may not charge both charts of one source as
independent errors.

§29.3 records the retired status of the unweighted per-`b` `C_joint ≤ 0.09` estimate.  The
reason is carried purely as metadata, and `unweightedCjoint_not_banked` makes it impossible
for a status file to import it from the banked list of closing estimates.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §29.1  Source typing -/

/-- The identifying data of a physical medium-`k` long-fibre source: the fibre modulus `b`,
the medium cutoff `K0`, the replayed edge cutoff and the lane offset. -/
structure LongFibreSourceId where
  /-- The fibre modulus. -/
  fibre : ℕ
  /-- The medium cutoff (`K0 = 31`). -/
  mediumCutoff : ℕ
  /-- The replayed edge cutoff (`50` previously, `1000` now). -/
  edgeCutoff : ℕ
  /-- The lane offset. -/
  lane : ℕ
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- The two available representations of one long-fibre source. -/
inductive ChartRepresentation
  | lambdaCovariance
  | allQResummation
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A ledger entry: a chart, the source it represents, and the charged amount. -/
structure ChartCharge where
  /-- Which representation is being charged. -/
  chart : ChartRepresentation
  /-- Which physical source it represents. -/
  source : LongFibreSourceId
  /-- The charged amount. -/
  amount : ℚ

/-- **`charts_same_source`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  With all hypotheses and cutoffs matching,
the λ-weighted covariance chart and the all-`q` resummation chart carry the *same* source:
they are two representations, not two sources. -/
theorem charts_same_source (S : LongFibreSourceId) (x y : ℚ) :
    (ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.lambdaCovariance S x).source
      = (ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.allQResummation S y).source := rfl

/-- **`charts_distinct_representations`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The two charts are genuinely
different representations, so the equality above is a statement about the *source* only. -/
theorem charts_distinct_representations :
    ChartRepresentation.lambdaCovariance ≠ ChartRepresentation.allQResummation := by decide

/-! ## §29.2  The double-charge firewall -/

/-- A ledger is *chart-legal* when no source is charged through two different charts. -/
def ChartLegal (L : List ChartCharge) : Prop :=
  ∀ c₁ ∈ L, ∀ c₂ ∈ L, c₁.source = c₂.source → c₁.chart = c₂.chart

/-- **`chart_double_charge_illegal`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Charging both charts of one source
as independent errors is never chart-legal. -/
theorem chart_double_charge_illegal (S : LongFibreSourceId) (x y : ℚ) :
    ¬ ChartLegal [ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.lambdaCovariance S x,
                  ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.allQResummation S y] := by
  intro h
  have hmem₁ : ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.lambdaCovariance S x ∈
      [ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.lambdaCovariance S x,
       ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.allQResummation S y] := by simp
  have hmem₂ : ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.allQResummation S y ∈
      [ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.lambdaCovariance S x,
       ChartCharge.mk ChartRepresentation.allQResummation S y] := by simp
  exact charts_distinct_representations (h _ hmem₁ _ hmem₂ rfl)

/-- **`chartLegal_single_chart`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  In a chart-legal ledger every charge
attached to a given source uses one and the same chart. -/
theorem chartLegal_single_chart {L : List ChartCharge} (h : ChartLegal L)
    {c₁ c₂ : ChartCharge} (h₁ : c₁ ∈ L) (h₂ : c₂ ∈ L) (hs : c₁.source = c₂.source) :
    c₁.chart = c₂.chart := h c₁ h₁ c₂ h₂ hs

/-- **`chartLegal_singleton`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Charging a source through exactly one
chart is legal — the firewall forbids double charging, not charging. -/
theorem chartLegal_singleton (c : ChartCharge) : ChartLegal [c] := by
  intro c₁ h₁ c₂ h₂ _
  simp only [List.mem_singleton] at h₁ h₂
  rw [h₁, h₂]

/-! ## §29.3  The retired-theorem firewall -/

/-- Identifiers for the estimates tracked by the effectivity bank. -/
inductive EstimateId
  | unweightedPerBCjoint009
  | completePeriodEndpointIdentity
  | allQResummationAlgebra
  | lambdaFiniteAlgebra
  | edgeReplacementSemantics
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Bank status of an estimate. -/
inductive BankStatus
  | banked
  | retired
  | openStatus
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Retirement reasons, carried as metadata only. -/
inductive RetirementReason
  | contradictedByOnePointFibre
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- The bank status of each tracked estimate. -/
def estimateStatus : EstimateId → BankStatus
  | .unweightedPerBCjoint009 => .retired
  | .completePeriodEndpointIdentity => .banked
  | .allQResummationAlgebra => .banked
  | .lambdaFiniteAlgebra => .banked
  | .edgeReplacementSemantics => .banked

/-- The retirement reason, as pure status metadata. -/
def retirementReason : EstimateId → Option RetirementReason
  | .unweightedPerBCjoint009 => some .contradictedByOnePointFibre
  | _ => none

/-- The list of estimates that may be imported as banked closing estimates. -/
def bankedClosingEstimates : List EstimateId :=
  [.completePeriodEndpointIdentity, .allQResummationAlgebra, .lambdaFiniteAlgebra,
   .edgeReplacementSemantics]

/-- **`unweightedCjoint_retired`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The unweighted per-`b`
`C_joint ≤ 0.09` estimate is recorded as retired, with its reason as metadata. -/
theorem unweightedCjoint_retired :
    estimateStatus .unweightedPerBCjoint009 = BankStatus.retired ∧
      retirementReason .unweightedPerBCjoint009 = some .contradictedByOnePointFibre :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl⟩

/-- **`unweightedCjoint_not_banked`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  It is impossible to import the
retired estimate as a banked closing estimate. -/
theorem unweightedCjoint_not_banked :
    EstimateId.unweightedPerBCjoint009 ∉ bankedClosingEstimates := by decide

/-- **`bankedClosingEstimates_are_banked`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Everything on the banked list
really has banked status. -/
theorem bankedClosingEstimates_are_banked :
    ∀ e ∈ bankedClosingEstimates, estimateStatus e = BankStatus.banked := by decide

/-- **`retired_ne_banked`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`. -/
theorem retired_ne_banked : BankStatus.retired ≠ BankStatus.banked := by decide

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=8210 sha256=424ce5458722eb21fcdc195350eb67c71beb4fb303e883b23da58f2c05524a6a path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/ChenP2Audit.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Chain

/-!
# Erdős Problem #287 — audit of the Chen / P₂ relaxation of the blocker pair

The certified blocker-pair contradiction (`Gap2CE.excludedPP_blockerPair`) forces two
adjacent holes `x, x+1 ∈ [N, M]` from two **excluded prime powers** `q₁ ∣ x`, `q₂ ∣ x+1`.
Exclusion is delivered by `primePower_window_exclusion`, whose proof is *intrinsically a
single-prime argument*: divisibility by `p^e` puts the element in the top `p`-adic layer,
whose reciprocal-sum numerator is bounded by `C(⌊M/p^e⌋)` yet must be divisible by `p`,
forcing it to vanish — a contradiction once `p > C(⌊M/p^e⌋)`.

This file audits whether **one side of the blocker pair can be relaxed from a prime power
`q` to a `P₂ = q₁·q₂`** (a semiprime, or more generally an almost-prime with controlled
prime factors) while still forcing a hole.

## Summary of the verdict (all machine-checked below)

* **Task 1.** We state the exact relaxed exclusion primitive `P2ForcesExclusion` and the
  relaxed blocker-pair theorem `RelaxedBlockerPair`.
* **Task 2/3.** The natural relaxation is **false**: `not_P2ForcesExclusion`. The concrete
  local configuration is `A = {2, 3, 6}` (`∑ 1/a = 1`) with `M = 6` and the semiprime
  `q = 6 = 2·3`.  Its "favourable" window `⌊M/q⌋ = 1` gives `C 1 = 1 < 2`, so the naive
  P₂ rule *predicts* a hole at `6`; yet `6 ∈ A`, so no hole is forced.
  `p2_window_illegitimate` pins down *why*: the top-layer argument only ever provides the
  window `⌊M/pᵢ⌋` of an *individual* prime factor, and for both factors of `6` that window
  fails to exclude (`C(⌊6/2⌋) = 11 ≥ 2`, `C(⌊6/3⌋) = 3 ≥ 3`).
* **Salvage.** The *only* sound way a `P₂` forces a hole is when one of its prime factors
  is *itself* an excluded prime power (`P2_excluded_via_prime_factor`) — but that reduces
  to the existing prime-power exclusion and is not a genuine relaxation.
* **Task 4.** Consequently a Chen-type theorem (infinitely many `p` with `p+2` a `P₂`) does
  **not** yield a usable infinite tail of blocker pairs: the `P₂` neighbour fails to force
  its hole. See `SFT_AUDIT.md` companion notes / the docstring of `chen_no_usable_tail`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287

/-! ## Task 1 — the relaxed exclusion primitive and relaxed blocker pair -/

/-- `q` is a `P₂` (semiprime): a product of two primes. -/
def IsP2 (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ p₁ p₂ : ℕ, p₁.Prime ∧ p₂.Prime ∧ q = p₁ * p₂

/-- The **naive P₂ exclusion predicate**: the literal analogue of `ExcludedPP` in which the
prime power `p^e` is replaced by a semiprime `q = p₁·p₂` (`p₁ ≤ p₂`), the window is the
*product's* window `⌊M/q⌋`, and the threshold is the smaller prime factor `p₁`.

This is the strongest/most favourable version of the relaxation: it uses the *smallest*
possible window `⌊M/q⌋` (making `C` small) and only demands the *smaller* prime factor to
beat it.  If even this fails to force exclusion, so does every weaker P₂ rule. -/
def ExcludedP2Naive (M q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ p₁ p₂ : ℕ, p₁.Prime ∧ p₂.Prime ∧ p₁ ≤ p₂ ∧ q = p₁ * p₂ ∧ C (M / q) < (p₁ : ℤ)

/-- **Task 1 — the exact relaxed exclusion claim.**  "A naively-excluded `P₂` forces a
hole": every element of a reciprocal-sum-`1` set `A ⊆ [1,M]` avoids multiples of a
naively-excluded semiprime `q`.  (Compare `ExcludedPP.not_dvd_mem`.) -/
def P2ForcesExclusion : Prop :=
  ∀ (M q : ℕ), ExcludedP2Naive M q →
    ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) → (∀ a ∈ A, a ≤ M) →
      (∑ a ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / a = 1) → ∀ x ∈ A, ¬ q ∣ x

/-- **Task 1 — the exact relaxed blocker-pair theorem.**  One side of the blocker pair is
relaxed from a prime power to a naively-excluded `P₂`; the other side stays an excluded
prime power.  This is the statement one would *want* in order to use a Chen-type pairing
(prime `p` next to a `P₂`). -/
def RelaxedBlockerPair : Prop :=
  ∀ (ce : Gap2CE) (x q₁ q₂ : ℕ),
    ce.N ≤ x → x + 1 ≤ ce.M →
    ExcludedP2Naive ce.M q₁ → ExcludedPP ce.M q₂ →
    q₁ ∣ x → q₂ ∣ (x + 1) → False

/-! ## Task 2 / 3 — the relaxation is false, with a concrete configuration

The natural P₂ exclusion primitive `P2ForcesExclusion` is refuted by the reciprocal-sum-`1`
configuration `A = {2, 3, 6}` and the semiprime `q = 6`. -/

/-- The witness set `A = {2, 3, 6}` has reciprocal sum `1`. -/
theorem p2_witness_sum : (∑ a ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ), (1 : ℚ) / a) = 1 := by
  norm_num

/-- `q = 6 = 2·3` is naively excluded on the window `[1, 6]`: its product window is
`⌊6/6⌋ = 1`, where `C 1 = 1 < 2`, the smaller prime factor. -/
theorem p2_six_excludedNaive : ExcludedP2Naive 6 6 := by
  refine ⟨2, 3, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, ?_⟩
  norm_num [C_one]

/-- **Task 2/3 result.**  The naive P₂ exclusion primitive is **false**: a semiprime that
is "naively excluded" can still divide a member of a reciprocal-sum-`1` set. -/
theorem not_P2ForcesExclusion : ¬ P2ForcesExclusion := by
  intro h
  -- Apply the claimed exclusion to A = {2,3,6}, M = 6, q = 6, x = 6.
  have hx : ¬ (6 : ℕ) ∣ 6 :=
    h 6 6 p2_six_excludedNaive ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ)
      (by intro a ha; fin_cases ha <;> norm_num)
      (by intro a ha; fin_cases ha <;> norm_num)
      p2_witness_sum 6 (by norm_num)
  exact hx (dvd_refl 6)

/-- **Why the relaxation fails.**  The single-prime top-layer argument can only ever offer
the window of an *individual* prime factor `pᵢ`, namely `⌊M/pᵢ⌋` — never the smaller
product window `⌊M/q⌋`.  For the counterexample `q = 6` on `[1,6]`, *both* legitimate
individual-prime windows fail to exclude:

* factor `2`: window `⌊6/2⌋ = 3`, `C 3 = 11 ≥ 2`;
* factor `3`: window `⌊6/3⌋ = 2`, `C 2 = 3 ≥ 3`.

So the exclusion is not merely unproven by our method — no member of the top-layer family
is genuinely excluded, matching the fact that `6 ∈ A`. -/
theorem p2_window_illegitimate :
    ¬ (C (6 / 2) < (2 : ℤ)) ∧ ¬ (C (6 / 3) < (3 : ℤ)) := by
  constructor
  · norm_num [C_three]
  · norm_num [C_two]

/-! ## Salvage — the only sound `P₂` blocker is a disguised prime-power blocker

A semiprime `q` *does* force a hole precisely when one of its prime factors is itself an
excluded prime power.  But then divisibility by that prime already excludes the element:
the "P₂" plays no role, so this is not a genuine relaxation. -/

/-- If a prime power `p₀` dividing the semiprime `q` is genuinely excluded on `[1,M]`, then
`q` cannot divide any member of a reciprocal-sum-`1` set `A ⊆ [1,M]`.  This is immediate
from `ExcludedPP.not_dvd_mem` (via `p₀ ∣ q ∣ x`) and shows the salvage adds nothing beyond
the prime-power case. -/
theorem P2_excluded_via_prime_factor {M q p₀ : ℕ} (hexc : ExcludedPP M p₀)
    (hpq : p₀ ∣ q) {A : Finset ℕ} (hpos : ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) (hAM : ∀ a ∈ A, a ≤ M)
    (hsum : ∑ a ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / a = 1) {x : ℕ} (hxA : x ∈ A) (hqx : q ∣ x) : False :=
  ExcludedPP.not_dvd_mem hexc hpos hAM hsum hxA (dvd_trans hpq hqx)

/-! ## Task 4 — no usable infinite tail from a Chen-type theorem

Chen-type theorems (e.g. infinitely many primes `p` with `p + 2` a `P₂`) supply an infinite
family of `(prime, P₂)` neighbours.  To convert such a family into an infinite tail of
blocker pairs one would need each `P₂` neighbour to *force its hole* via
`RelaxedBlockerPair`.  But `not_P2ForcesExclusion` shows the `P₂` side does **not** force a
hole in general, so the tail collapses: the prime side gives one hole, the `P₂` side gives
none, and no adjacent double hole is produced.

We record this as: `RelaxedBlockerPair` would entail `P2ForcesExclusion`-style exclusion,
which is false.  Concretely, any purported "Chen tail" theorem that produced a hole from a
naively-excluded `P₂` would contradict `not_P2ForcesExclusion` on the local configuration
`{2,3,6}`.  Hence no Chen-type input yields a usable infinite tail through this mechanism. -/
theorem chen_no_usable_tail :
    ¬ P2ForcesExclusion := not_P2ForcesExclusion

end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=6620 sha256=49b358431b9337dd725b034c184a00dfcf2cd139662a54a7ca558104514f1710 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/ClosureInputs.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.FiniteRangeExtension

/-!
# Erdős Problem #287 — the exact remaining input, and the end-to-end compiler

Everything finite in this development is now packaged behind **one** predicate.

`WindowPairSupply M` says: there is a position `x` with `M/2 ≤ x < M` such that both `x`
and `x + 1` carry a prime power `p^e` whose window `⌊M/p^e⌋` is at most `9` and whose base
exceeds the certified numerator bound `C ⌊M/p^e⌋`.  By `Gap2CE.blocker_window` this single
condition refutes every counterexample with maximum `M`
(`Gap2CE.no_of_windowPairSupply`).

Three facts about this interface:

* it is **implied by** a (sign-sensitive) Sophie witness at `M`
  (`windowPairSupply_of_sophieWitness`), so it is a *weaker* — hence more plausible —
  arithmetic supply statement than the Sophie-Germain-type condition used previously;
* it holds for every `3 ≤ M ≤ 4·10⁹` by the kernel-checked certificate chain of
  `FiniteRangeExtension.lean`;
* it is **not proved here for large `M`**, and nothing in this project asserts it.  In the
  size range that matters, `⌊M/p^e⌋ ≤ 9` forces `p^e > M/10`, so the statement asks for two
  consecutive integers just above `M/2`, each with a prime-power divisor of size `≫ M`.
  Proving that for all large `M` is an analytic problem of Ford–Maynard type; it is *not*
  proved in this repository and is not assumed as an axiom anywhere.

`Erdos287ClosureInputs` bundles exactly the missing item together with an explicit,
effective threshold, and `no_Erdos287Counterexample_of_closure` compiles it into the exact
public statement.  No field of the structure is (or implies by definition) the conclusion:
the single mathematical field is the supply statement above the threshold.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287

/-- **The exact public statement of Erdős #287** (set form). -/
def Erdos287Statement : Prop := ∀ A : Finset ℕ, ¬ Erdos287Counterexample A

/-- **The window-pair supply at `M`.**  Two consecutive positions `x`, `x+1` in the top
half of `[1, M]`, each divisible by a prime power whose window at `M` is at most `9` and
whose base beats the certified numerator bound of that window. -/
def WindowPairSupply (M : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ x pu au pv av : ℕ,
    pu.Prime ∧ pv.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ au ∧ 1 ≤ av ∧
    pu ^ au ∣ x ∧ pv ^ av ∣ (x + 1) ∧
    M / pu ^ au ≤ 9 ∧ CVal (M / pu ^ au) < pu ∧
    M / pv ^ av ≤ 9 ∧ CVal (M / pv ^ av) < pv ∧
    M ≤ 2 * x ∧ x + 1 ≤ M

namespace Gap2CE

variable (ce : Gap2CE)

/-- A window-pair supply at the maximum refutes the counterexample. -/
theorem no_of_windowPairSupply (h : WindowPairSupply ce.M) : False := by
  obtain ⟨x, pu, au, pv, av, hpu, hpv, hau, hav, hdu, hdv, hwu, hcu, hwv, hcv, hUx, hxL⟩ := h
  exact ce.blocker_window hpu hpv hau hav hdu hdv hwu hcu hwv hcv hUx hxL le_rfl le_rfl

end Gap2CE

/-- Division bound used below: `M < (c+1)·k` gives `⌊M/k⌋ ≤ c`. -/
theorem div_le_of_lt_mul {M k c : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (h : M < (c + 1) * k) : M / k ≤ c := by
  have := (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hk).2 h
  omega

/-- `CVal` at windows `0, 1` is `1`. -/
theorem CVal_eq_one_of_le_one {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ 1) : CVal j = 1 := by
  interval_cases j <;> norm_num [CVal]

/-- `CVal` at windows `≤ 2` is at most `3`. -/
theorem CVal_le_three_of_le_two {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ 2) : CVal j ≤ 3 := by
  interval_cases j <;> norm_num [CVal]

/-- **The Sophie interface is stronger than the window-pair interface.**  Every
sign-sensitive Sophie witness at `M` yields a window pair at `M`: for a plus witness take
`x = 2q` (window `2`, and `C 2 = 3 < q`) with `x + 1 = 2q + 1` prime (window `1`); for a
minus witness take `x = 2q - 1` prime (window `1`) with `x + 1 = 2q` (window `2`). -/
theorem windowPairSupply_of_sophieWitness {M : ℕ} (h : SophieWitness M) :
    WindowPairSupply M := by
  rcases h with ⟨q, hq, hq5, hM3, hfit, hp⟩ | ⟨q, hq, hq5, hM3, hfit, hp⟩
  · -- plus witness: `x = 2q`, `x + 1 = 2q + 1`
    have hwu : M / q ^ 1 ≤ 2 := by
      rw [pow_one]; exact div_le_of_lt_mul (by omega) (by omega)
    have hwv : M / (2 * q + 1) ^ 1 ≤ 1 := by
      rw [pow_one]; exact div_le_of_lt_mul (by omega) (by omega)
    refine ⟨2 * q, q, 1, 2 * q + 1, 1, hq, hp, le_rfl, le_rfl, ⟨2, by rw [pow_one]; ring⟩,
      ⟨1, by rw [pow_one, mul_one]⟩, by omega, ?_, by omega, ?_, by omega, by omega⟩
    · have := CVal_le_three_of_le_two hwu; omega
    · have := CVal_eq_one_of_le_one hwv; omega
  · -- minus witness: `x = 2q - 1`, `x + 1 = 2q`
    have hwu : M / (2 * q - 1) ^ 1 ≤ 1 := by
      rw [pow_one]; exact div_le_of_lt_mul (by omega) (by omega)
    have hwv : M / q ^ 1 ≤ 2 := by
      rw [pow_one]; exact div_le_of_lt_mul (by omega) (by omega)
    refine ⟨2 * q - 1, 2 * q - 1, 1, q, 1, hp, hq, le_rfl, le_rfl,
      ⟨1, by rw [pow_one, mul_one]⟩, ⟨2, by rw [pow_one]; omega⟩,
      by omega, ?_, by omega, ?_, by omega, by omega⟩
    · have := CVal_eq_one_of_le_one hwu; omega
    · have := CVal_le_three_of_le_two hwv; omega

/-- **The end-to-end closure inputs.**  Exactly one mathematical field: the window-pair
supply above an explicit threshold that lies inside the kernel-verified finite range.
No field is the conclusion, and no field mentions counterexamples. -/
structure Erdos287ClosureInputs where
  /-- An explicit, effective threshold. -/
  M0 : ℕ
  /-- The threshold lies inside the kernel-verified finite range `[3, 4·10⁹]`. -/
  threshold_covered : M0 ≤ 4000000000
  /-- The supply statement above the threshold.  **Not proved in this repository.** -/
  supply : ∀ M : ℕ, M0 ≤ M → WindowPairSupply M

/-- **End-to-end compiler.**  The closure inputs imply the exact public statement. -/
theorem no_Erdos287Counterexample_of_closure (I : Erdos287ClosureInputs) :
    Erdos287Statement := by
  intro A h
  by_cases hM : A.max' h.nonempty ≤ 4000000000
  · exact no_Erdos287Counterexample_of_max_le_4e9 h hM
  · refine (h.toGap2CE).no_of_windowPairSupply ?_
    exact I.supply _ (by
      show I.M0 ≤ A.max' h.nonempty
      have := I.threshold_covered
      omega)

/-- **Ordered (public) form of the same compiler.** -/
theorem erdos287_seq_of_closure (I : Erdos287ClosureInputs)
    (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hmono : ∀ i j, i < j → j < k → n i < n j)
    (hone : ∀ i, i < k → 1 < n i)
    (hsum : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, (1 : ℚ) / (n i) = 1) :
    ∃ i, i + 1 < k ∧ n i + 3 ≤ n (i + 1) :=
  erdos287_seq_of_no_counterexample (no_Erdos287Counterexample_of_closure I) k n hmono hone hsum

end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=11353 sha256=fc5e25481b5bb18f47134b6472f79955539b6e774f77e359a21064238c9255ae path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/CompensatedMeasure.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.BsrcWeights
import RequestProject.Erdos287.ProperGammaOddConvolution

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — the compensated counting measure `G_M`, `Ĝ_M`, `Ê_M` (§50)

```
HYPERBOLA DOUBLE-SUM IDENTITY          : KERNEL-PROVED
ODD CONVOLUTION t·β(t) = 1_odd ⋆ η     : KERNEL-PROVED (reuses the banked η)
G_M IN CONVOLUTION FORM                : KERNEL-PROVED
EXACT FINITE EXPRESSION FOR Ê_M        : KERNEL-PROVED
PER-ATOM COMPENSATION BOUND |ρ| ≤ 1/2  : KERNEL-PROVED
INFINITE TAIL                          : CONDITIONAL_ANALYTIC (hypothesis, not asserted)
```

This module is **append-only**: nothing in the long-fibre, proper-γ, multiplicity or
EARLY_4490 banks is rewritten.  It reuses `beta`, `gz` and `hz` verbatim from
`BsrcWeights` / `ProperGammaOddConvolution`.

The selected β-weight is

    w(t) = t · β(t),

and the banked local coefficients are `η = hz 1` (the odd-supported Möbius transform of
`g_1(t) = t β(t)`), for which the banked identity `oddConvolution_identity` gives exactly

    t β(t) = (1_odd ⋆ η)(t).

The compensated measure is then defined at integer cut-off `Y`:

    G_M(Y)  = ∑_{1 ≤ t ≤ Y} t β(t) 1_{(t,M)=1},
    Ĝ_M(Y)  = ∑_{1 ≤ d ≤ Y} η_M(d) · Y/(2d),
    Ê_M(Y)  = G_M(Y) − Ĝ_M(Y).

`Ehat_exact` gives the exact finite expression of `Ê_M(Y)` as the sum of the atomwise
compensation defects, each of absolute value at most `1/2`.  **No smallness of `Ê_M` is
asserted**: the only bound proved is the trivial `ℓ¹` bound, and the infinite-cut-off
statement is carried as an explicit hypothesis object.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §50.1  The hyperbola double-sum identity -/

/-- The hyperbola region `{(d,u) : d,u ≥ 1, d·u ≤ Y}`. -/
def hyperbolaRegion (Y : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  (Finset.Icc 1 Y ×ˢ Finset.Icc 1 Y).filter (fun q => q.1 * q.2 ≤ Y)

lemma mem_hyperbolaRegion {Y : ℕ} {q : ℕ × ℕ} :
    q ∈ hyperbolaRegion Y ↔ 1 ≤ q.1 ∧ 1 ≤ q.2 ∧ q.1 * q.2 ≤ Y := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    simp only [hyperbolaRegion, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Icc] at h
    exact ⟨h.1.1.1, h.1.2.1, h.2⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
    have hq1 : q.1 ≤ Y := le_trans (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ h2) h3
    have hq2 : q.2 ≤ Y := le_trans (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ h1) h3
    simp only [hyperbolaRegion, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Icc]
    exact ⟨⟨⟨h1, hq1⟩, ⟨h2, hq2⟩⟩, h3⟩

/-- The fibre of the hyperbola region over a product value `t ≥ 1`, `t ≤ Y`, is exactly the
divisor antidiagonal of `t`. -/
lemma hyperbolaRegion_fiber {Y t : ℕ} (ht1 : 1 ≤ t) (htY : t ≤ Y) :
    (hyperbolaRegion Y).filter (fun q => q.1 * q.2 = t) = t.divisorsAntidiagonal := by
  ext q
  simp only [Finset.mem_filter, mem_hyperbolaRegion, Nat.mem_divisorsAntidiagonal]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨-, h⟩; exact ⟨h, by omega⟩
  · rintro ⟨hmul, -⟩
    have h1 : 1 ≤ q.1 := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos q.1 with h | h
      · simp [h] at hmul; omega
      · exact h
    have h2 : 1 ≤ q.2 := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos q.2 with h | h
      · simp [h] at hmul; omega
      · exact h
    exact ⟨⟨h1, h2, by omega⟩, hmul⟩

/-- **`hyperbola_double_sum`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact hyperbola interchange

    ∑_{t ≤ Y} ∑_{d ∣ t} f(d) g(t/d) = ∑_{d ≤ Y} f(d) ∑_{u ≤ Y/d} g(u).

No estimate is involved: this is an exact reindexing of a finite sum. -/
theorem hyperbola_double_sum (Y : ℕ) (f g : ℕ → ℚ) :
    ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, ∑ d ∈ t.divisors, f d * g (t / d)
      = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, f d * ∑ u ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Y / d), g u := by
  have hmaps : ∀ q ∈ hyperbolaRegion Y, q.1 * q.2 ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y := by
    intro q hq
    rw [mem_hyperbolaRegion] at hq
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := hq
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc]
    exact ⟨Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 (Nat.mul_ne_zero (by omega) (by omega)), h3⟩
  have hgroup :
      ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, ∑ q ∈ (hyperbolaRegion Y).filter (fun q => q.1 * q.2 = t),
          f q.1 * g q.2
        = ∑ q ∈ hyperbolaRegion Y, f q.1 * g q.2 :=
    Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps _
  have hleft :
      ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, ∑ d ∈ t.divisors, f d * g (t / d)
        = ∑ q ∈ hyperbolaRegion Y, f q.1 * g q.2 := by
    rw [← hgroup]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun t ht => ?_
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at ht
    rw [hyperbolaRegion_fiber ht.1 ht.2, ← Nat.sum_divisorsAntidiagonal (fun a b => f a * g b)]
  have hright :
      ∑ q ∈ hyperbolaRegion Y, f q.1 * g q.2
        = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, f d * ∑ u ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Y / d), g u := by
    rw [hyperbolaRegion, Finset.sum_filter,
      Finset.sum_product' (Finset.Icc 1 Y) (Finset.Icc 1 Y)
        (fun x y => if x * y ≤ Y then f x * g y else 0)]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d hd => ?_
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at hd
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    have hset : Finset.Icc 1 (Y / d) = (Finset.Icc 1 Y).filter (fun u => d * u ≤ Y) := by
      ext u
      simp only [Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_filter]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hu1, hu2⟩
        have hdu : d * u ≤ Y := by
          rw [mul_comm]; exact (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le (by omega)).1 hu2
        refine ⟨⟨hu1, ?_⟩, hdu⟩
        exact le_trans (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ (by omega)) hdu
      · rintro ⟨⟨hu1, -⟩, hdu⟩
        refine ⟨hu1, (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le (by omega)).2 ?_⟩
        rw [mul_comm]; exact hdu
    rw [hset, Finset.sum_filter]
  rw [hleft, hright]

/-! ## §50.2  The selected β-weight and its banked local coefficients -/

/-- The selected weight `w(t) = t·β(t)`. -/
def wbeta (t : ℕ) : ℚ := (t : ℚ) * beta t

/-- The banked local coefficients `η = h_1`, the odd-supported Möbius transform of `w`. -/
def etaLoc (d : ℕ) : ℚ := hz 1 d

lemma gz_one_eq_wbeta (t : ℕ) : gz 1 t = wbeta t := by
  simp [gz, wbeta]

/-- **`selectedWeight_oddConvolution`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The odd-convolution identity
`t·β(t) = (1_odd ⋆ η)(t)` with the banked local coefficients `η`. -/
theorem selectedWeight_oddConvolution {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, (if ¬ 2 ∣ (n / d) then (1 : ℚ) else 0) * etaLoc d = wbeta n := by
  rw [← gz_one_eq_wbeta]
  exact oddConvolution_identity 1 hn

/-! ## §50.3  The compensated counting measure -/

/-- `G_M(Y) = ∑_{1 ≤ t ≤ Y} t β(t) 1_{(t,M)=1}` — the selected counting measure. -/
def GM (M Y : ℕ) : ℚ := ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, gz M t

/-- The `M`-restricted local coefficients. -/
def etaM (M d : ℕ) : ℚ := hz M d

/-- The smooth (density) part `Ĝ_M(Y) = ∑_{d ≤ Y} η_M(d)·Y/(2d)`. -/
def GhatM (M Y : ℕ) : ℚ := ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, etaM M d * ((Y : ℚ) / (2 * d))

/-- The compensated remainder `Ê_M(Y) = G_M(Y) − Ĝ_M(Y)`. -/
def EhatM (M Y : ℕ) : ℚ := GM M Y - GhatM M Y

/-- The atomwise compensation defect at cut-off `Y` and modulus `d`:
`ρ(Y,d) = #{odd u ≤ Y/d} − Y/(2d)`. -/
def rhoAtom (Y d : ℕ) : ℚ := (((Y / d + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) - (Y : ℚ) / (2 * d)

/-- **`GM_convolution_form`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The measure in local-coefficient form:

    G_M(Y) = ∑_{d ≤ Y} η_M(d) · #{odd u ≤ Y/d}. -/
theorem GM_convolution_form (M Y : ℕ) :
    GM M Y = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, etaM M d * (((Y / d + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
  have hexp : GM M Y
      = ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, ∑ d ∈ t.divisors,
          etaM M d * (if ¬ 2 ∣ (t / d) then (1 : ℚ) else 0) := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun t ht => ?_
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at ht
    rw [← oddConvolution_identity M (by omega)]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => by rw [mul_comm]; rfl
  rw [hexp, hyperbola_double_sum Y (fun d => etaM M d)
    (fun u => if ¬ 2 ∣ u then (1 : ℚ) else 0)]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => ?_
  congr 1
  rw [Finset.sum_boole, oddCount_exact (Y / d)]

/-- **`Ehat_exact`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact finite expression of the compensated
remainder as a sum of atomwise defects.  No smallness is asserted. -/
theorem Ehat_exact (M Y : ℕ) :
    EhatM M Y = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, etaM M d * rhoAtom Y d := by
  rw [EhatM, GM_convolution_form, GhatM, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => ?_
  rw [rhoAtom, mul_sub]

/-- **`abs_rhoAtom_le`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Each atomwise defect is bounded by `1/2`. -/
theorem abs_rhoAtom_le {Y d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) : |rhoAtom Y d| ≤ 1 / 2 := by
  have hkey : Y < (Y / d + 1) * d := by
    have h1 := Nat.div_add_mod Y d
    have h2 := Nat.mod_lt Y hd
    nlinarith
  have hqd : ((Y / d : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ (Y : ℚ) / d := by
    rw [le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
    exact_mod_cast Nat.div_mul_le_self Y d
  have hqd' : (Y : ℚ) / d < ((Y / d : ℕ) : ℚ) + 1 := by
    rw [div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]
    exact_mod_cast hkey
  have hcount : ((Y / d + 1) / 2 : ℕ) * 2 ≤ Y / d + 1 ∧ Y / d ≤ ((Y / d + 1) / 2 : ℕ) * 2 := by
    omega
  have h1 : (((Y / d + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) * 2 ≤ ((Y / d : ℕ) : ℚ) + 1 := by exact_mod_cast hcount.1
  have h2 : ((Y / d : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ (((Y / d + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) * 2 := by exact_mod_cast hcount.2
  have hhalf : (Y : ℚ) / (2 * d) = ((Y : ℚ) / d) / 2 := by
    rw [div_div]; ring_nf
  rw [abs_le, rhoAtom, hhalf]
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- **`abs_Ehat_le_l1`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The only bound proved here is the trivial
`ℓ¹` bound `|Ê_M(Y)| ≤ (1/2) ∑_{d ≤ Y} |η_M(d)|`.  This is *not* a smallness statement. -/
theorem abs_Ehat_le_l1 (M Y : ℕ) :
    |EhatM M Y| ≤ (1 / 2) * ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, |etaM M d| := by
  rw [Ehat_exact, Finset.mul_sum]
  refine le_trans (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _) (Finset.sum_le_sum fun d hd => ?_)
  rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at hd
  rw [abs_mul]
  have h := abs_rhoAtom_le (Y := Y) (d := d) (by omega)
  have habs : (0 : ℚ) ≤ |etaM M d| := abs_nonneg _
  calc |etaM M d| * |rhoAtom Y d| ≤ |etaM M d| * (1 / 2) := by
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h habs
    _ = 1 / 2 * |etaM M d| := by ring

/-! ## §50.4  The infinite cut-off: conditional interface only -/

/-- The infinite-cut-off statement for the compensated measure is carried as an explicit
hypothesis object: a limit of the finite truncations.  It is **never** asserted, and no
external analytic estimate is imported. -/
structure CompensatedTailInterface (M : ℕ) where
  /-- the claimed limit of the compensated remainders along a scaling -/
  limitValue : ℝ
  /-- the hypothesis that the finite truncations converge to it -/
  tendsto :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun Y : ℕ => ((EhatM M Y : ℚ) : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds limitValue)

/-- **`compensated_tail_not_asserted`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Inhabiting the tail interface
carries no numerical content: for every real `c` there is a hypothesis object with that
limit value *if* the corresponding convergence holds.  Nothing here proves convergence. -/
theorem compensated_tail_not_asserted (M : ℕ) (I : CompensatedTailInterface M) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun Y : ℕ => ((EhatM M Y : ℚ) : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds I.limitValue) :=
  I.tendsto

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.CompensatedMeasure
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Early4490FiniteACompiler

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — compensated summation by parts (§52)

```
COMPENSATED SUMMATION BY PARTS (exact) : KERNEL-PROVED
PRINCIPAL / ENDPOINT / Ê / JUMP SPLIT  : KERNEL-PROVED
NO SMALLNESS OF THE ERROR TERMS        : FIREWALL (explicit nonzero Ê witness)
```

The identity formalised here is the **exact discrete** compensated summation by parts on the
window `1 ≤ a ≤ Y`, in the strict Bernoulli endpoint convention already used by the bank
(the atom `a` carries the increment `G(a) − G(a−1)`, the endpoint contribution is evaluated
at the right endpoint and the lower endpoint enters through `G(0) = 0`):

    ∑_{1 ≤ a ≤ Y} a β(a) 1_{(a,M)=1} H(a)
        =  [ Ĝ_M(Y) H(Y) − ∑_{1 ≤ a < Y} Ĝ_M(a) ΔH(a) ]     (principal part)
         +   Ê_M(Y) H(Y)                                      (endpoint Ê term)
         − ∑_{1 ≤ a < Y} Ê_M(a) H'_reg(a)                     (regularised Ê term)
         − ∑_{1 ≤ a < Y} Ê_M(a) J(a)                          (hyperbola-interface jumps)

where the test increment splits as `ΔH(a) = H(a+1) − H(a) = H'_reg(a) + J(a)`, the jump part
`J` being supported on the hyperbola interfaces.  The continuous (integral) form of the same
identity is **not** claimed: it needs analytic integration by parts against a step measure and
is not reconstructed here.

**No error term is asserted to be small.**  `sbp_no_smallness_asserted` exhibits an explicit
finite instance in which the endpoint `Ê` term is nonzero.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §52.1  The four parts -/

/-- The principal (density) part of the compensated summation by parts. -/
def sbpPrincipal (M : ℕ) (H : ℕ → ℚ) (Y : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  GhatM M Y * H Y - ∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, GhatM M a * (H (a + 1) - H a)

/-- The endpoint `Ê` term. -/
def sbpEndpoint (M : ℕ) (H : ℕ → ℚ) (Y : ℕ) : ℚ := EhatM M Y * H Y

/-- The regularised `Ê` term (the discrete analogue of `∫ Ê H'_reg`). -/
def sbpEhatReg (M : ℕ) (Hreg : ℕ → ℚ) (Y : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, EhatM M a * Hreg a

/-- The hyperbola-interface jump sum. -/
def sbpJump (M : ℕ) (J : ℕ → ℚ) (Y : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, EhatM M a * J a

@[simp] lemma GM_zero (M : ℕ) : GM M 0 = 0 := by simp [GM]

@[simp] lemma GhatM_zero (M : ℕ) : GhatM M 0 = 0 := by simp [GhatM]

@[simp] lemma EhatM_zero (M : ℕ) : EhatM M 0 = 0 := by simp [EhatM]

lemma GM_succ_sub (M a : ℕ) : GM M (a + 1) - GM M a = gz M (a + 1) := by
  rw [GM, GM, Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega)]
  ring

lemma GM_sub_pred {M a : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) : GM M a - GM M (a - 1) = gz M a := by
  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ : ∃ b, a = b + 1 := ⟨a - 1, by omega⟩
  simpa using GM_succ_sub M b

/-! ## §52.2  The exact identity -/

/-- **`compensated_summation_by_parts`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact four-term compensated
summation by parts, in the strict Bernoulli endpoint convention.  The hypothesis `hsplit`
is the definition of the regularised increment and the interface jump; no estimate of any
term is asserted. -/
theorem compensated_summation_by_parts (M : ℕ) (H Hreg J : ℕ → ℚ) {Y : ℕ} (hY : 1 ≤ Y)
    (hsplit : ∀ a, H (a + 1) - H a = Hreg a + J a) :
    ∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, gz M a * H a
      = sbpPrincipal M H Y + sbpEndpoint M H Y - sbpEhatReg M Hreg Y - sbpJump M J Y := by
  have habel :
      ∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, (GM M a - GM M (a - 1)) * H a
        = GM M Y * H Y - GM M (1 - 1) * H 1
            - ∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, GM M a * (H (a + 1) - H a) :=
    abel_summation_general (GM M) H hY
  have hleft : ∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, gz M a * H a
      = ∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, (GM M a - GM M (a - 1)) * H a := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at ha
    rw [GM_sub_pred ha.1]
  have hGsplit : ∀ a, GM M a = GhatM M a + EhatM M a := by
    intro a; rw [EhatM]; ring
  rw [hleft, habel]
  simp only [Nat.sub_self, GM_zero, zero_mul, sub_zero]
  rw [sbpPrincipal, sbpEndpoint, sbpEhatReg, sbpJump, hGsplit Y]
  have hsum : ∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, GM M a * (H (a + 1) - H a)
      = (∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, GhatM M a * (H (a + 1) - H a))
        + (∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, EhatM M a * Hreg a)
        + (∑ a ∈ Finset.Ico 1 Y, EhatM M a * J a) := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    rw [hGsplit a, hsplit a]
    ring
  rw [hsum]
  ring

/-! ## §52.3  Firewall: no smallness is asserted -/

lemma gz_one_eq_one (M : ℕ) : gz M 1 = 1 := by
  simp [gz]

lemma etaM_one (M : ℕ) : etaM M 1 = 1 := by
  have h : hzRaw M 1 = 1 := by
    rw [hzRaw]
    norm_num [gz, Nat.coprime_one_left]
  simp [etaM, hz, h]

/-- **`sbp_no_smallness_asserted`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The compensated remainder is not
small by fiat: at `M = 1`, `Y = 1` the endpoint compensation equals `1/2 ≠ 0`, so the exact
identity above carries no bound on any of its terms. -/
theorem sbp_no_smallness_asserted : EhatM 1 1 = 1 / 2 ∧ EhatM 1 1 ≠ 0 := by
  have hG : GM 1 1 = 1 := by simp [GM, gz_one_eq_one]
  have hGh : GhatM 1 1 = 1 / 2 := by
    rw [GhatM]
    norm_num [etaM_one]
  refine ⟨by rw [EhatM, hG, hGh]; norm_num, ?_⟩
  rw [EhatM, hG, hGh]; norm_num

end Effectivity
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=9095 sha256=653e5145d1e51b5569bde1b978fbda58106f31febf20fdde6b5aec689e377bef path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/CompensationLoop.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.SmallEllCRT
import RequestProject.Erdos287.HalfOpenProgressionCompiler

/-!
# Erdős #287 effectivity — the exact compensation loop (§59)

```
ell ≤ 1000 ATOMWISE CANCELLATION      : KERNEL-PROVED
RETURNED FINITE-CONDUCTOR KERNEL      : KERNEL-PROVED DEFINITION + COMPILER FORM
RETURNED KERNEL NOT IDENTICALLY ZERO  : KERNEL-PROVED
REASSEMBLY = EXACT LOOP, NOT CLOSURE  : KERNEL-PROVED FIREWALL (HIGH PRIORITY)
```

The banked source has already removed the conductor range `ℓ ≤ 1000`.  Writing
`bankedAtom` for the banked (already-removed) part and `Kell` for the internal atom, the
compensated atom is

    compAtom ℓ = K_ℓ − bankedAtom ℓ,     bankedAtom ℓ = if ℓ ≤ 1000 then K_ℓ else 0,

so `compAtom` vanishes identically on `ℓ ≤ 1000` (`loop_cancellation_le_1000`): that range
lies outside the original conductor support and cancels internally.  What survives is the
**returned finite-conductor kernel** on `1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000`, which via the compiler is the
finite object `∑_{1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000} Q_ℓ(A,B;z)`.

**Firewall (high priority).**  `reassembly_exact_loop` records that reassembling the returned
kernel into the original conductor expression is an *exact loop*: the difference is
identically `0`, so it yields no bound, while `returnedKernel_not_identically_zero` shows the
returned kernel is not the zero object.  Closure therefore requires a genuinely new analytic
input, not a reassembly.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace Erdos287
namespace Effectivity

/-! ## §59.1  Atomwise compensation -/

/-- The banked (already-removed) atom: supported on the old conductor range `ℓ ≤ 1000`. -/
def bankedAtom (ell : ℕ) (s z : ℤ) : ℚ := if ell ≤ 1000 then Kell ell s z else 0

/-- The compensated atom. -/
def compAtom (ell : ℕ) (s z : ℤ) : ℚ := Kell ell s z - bankedAtom ell s z

/-- **`loop_cancellation_le_1000`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Every atom with `ℓ ≤ 1000` cancels
internally: it lies outside the original conductor support. -/
theorem loop_cancellation_le_1000 {ell : ℕ} (h : ell ≤ 1000) (s z : ℤ) :
    compAtom ell s z = 0 := by
  rw [compAtom, bankedAtom, if_pos h, sub_self]

/-- **`compAtom_gt_1000`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Above the old conductor range the compensated
atom is the full local kernel. -/
theorem compAtom_gt_1000 {ell : ℕ} (h : ¬ ell ≤ 1000) (s z : ℤ) :
    compAtom ell s z = Kell ell s z := by
  rw [compAtom, bankedAtom, if_neg h, sub_zero]

/-! ## §59.2  The returned finite-conductor kernel -/

/-- The returned finite-conductor kernel on `1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000`, in compiled form. -/
def returnedKernel (A B z : ℤ) : ℚ := ∑ ell ∈ Finset.Icc 1001 5000, Qell ell A B z

/-- **`returnedKernel_eq_compensated_sum`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Summing the compensated atoms
over the whole internal range `1 ≤ ℓ ≤ 5000` returns exactly the finite-conductor kernel:
everything below `1000` has cancelled. -/
theorem returnedKernel_eq_compensated_sum (A B z : ℤ) :
    ∑ ell ∈ Finset.Icc 1 5000, ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, compAtom ell s z
      = returnedKernel A B z := by
  classical
  have hsplit : ∑ ell ∈ Finset.Icc 1 5000, ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, compAtom ell s z
      = ∑ ell ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 5000).filter (fun ell => ¬ ell ≤ 1000),
          ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, compAtom ell s z := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not (Finset.Icc 1 5000) (fun ell => ell ≤ 1000)]
    have hzero : ∑ ell ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 5000).filter (fun ell => ell ≤ 1000),
        ∑ s ∈ Finset.Ico A B, compAtom ell s z = 0 := by
      refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun ell hell => ?_
      rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hell
      exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun s _ => loop_cancellation_le_1000 hell.2 s z
    rw [hzero, zero_add]
  have hset : (Finset.Icc 1 5000).filter (fun ell => ¬ ell ≤ 1000) = Finset.Icc 1001 5000 := by
    ext ell
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc]
    omega
  rw [hsplit, hset, returnedKernel]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ell hell => ?_
  rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at hell
  have hgt : ¬ ell ≤ 1000 := by omega
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun s _ => compAtom_gt_1000 hgt s z),
    Qell_compiler (by omega : 0 < ell) A B z]

/-! ## §59.3  The returned kernel is not zero -/

lemma gcdFactors_prime {ell p : ℕ} (hell : ell ≠ 0) (hp : p.Prime) (hdvd : p ∣ ell) :
    gcdFactors ell (p : ℤ) = {p} := by
  ext q
  simp only [gcdFactors, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_singleton, Nat.mem_primeFactors]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨⟨hq, -, -⟩, hqp⟩
    have : q ∣ p := by exact_mod_cast hqp
    exact (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hq hp).1 this
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨⟨hp, hdvd, hell⟩, dvd_rfl⟩

lemma coprimeMask_one (ell : ℕ) : coprimeMask ell 1 = 1 := by
  refine Finset.prod_eq_one fun q hq => ?_
  have hq2 := (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hq).two_le
  have : ¬ ((q : ℤ) ∣ 1) := by
    intro h
    have hq1 : q ∣ 1 := by exact_mod_cast h
    have := Nat.dvd_one.mp hq1
    omega
  simp [this]

lemma cEll_ne_zero {ell : ℕ} (hsq : Squarefree ell) (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ ell) : cEll ell ≠ 0 := by
  have hmu : ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius ell : ℤ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    have h := (ArithmeticFunction.moebius_ne_zero_iff_squarefree (n := ell)).2 hsq
    exact_mod_cast h
  have hbeta : beta ell ≠ 0 := by
    rw [beta_of_odd_squarefree hsq hodd]
    have hprod : ∏ p ∈ ell.primeFactors, ((p : ℚ) - 2) ≠ 0 := by
      refine Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.2 fun p hp => ?_
      have hprime := Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp
      have hpd := Nat.dvd_of_mem_primeFactors hp
      have hp2 : p ≠ 2 := by
        intro h
        exact hodd (h ▸ hpd)
      have hp3 : 3 ≤ p := by have := hprime.two_le; omega
      have : (3 : ℚ) ≤ (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hp3
      intro hc
      have := sub_eq_zero.1 hc
      linarith
    exact one_div_ne_zero hprod
  have hphi : ((Nat.totient ell : ℕ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    have := Nat.totient_pos.2 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hsq.ne_zero)
    exact_mod_cast this.ne'
  rw [cEll]
  exact div_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero hmu hbeta) hphi

/-- **`Kell_ne_zero_at_prime_atom`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For odd squarefree `ℓ` and a prime
`p ∣ ℓ`, the atom `s = p`, `z = p + 1` gives a nonzero local kernel. -/
theorem Kell_ne_zero_at_prime_atom {ell p : ℕ} (hsq : Squarefree ell) (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ ell)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hdvd : p ∣ ell) :
    Kell ell (p : ℤ) ((p : ℤ) + 1) ≠ 0 := by
  have hell0 : ell ≠ 0 := hsq.ne_zero
  have hsub : ((p : ℤ) + 1) - (p : ℤ) = 1 := by ring
  rw [Kell, hsub, coprimeMask_one, gcdFactors_prime hell0 hp hdvd, Finset.prod_singleton, mul_one]
  have hbr : (2 - (p : ℚ)) - 1 ≠ 0 := by
    have : (2 : ℚ) ≤ (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hp.two_le
    intro h
    have : (p : ℚ) = 1 := by linarith [sub_eq_zero.1 h]
    have h2 : (2 : ℚ) ≤ 1 := by rw [← this]; exact_mod_cast hp.two_le
    linarith
  exact mul_ne_zero (cEll_ne_zero hsq hodd) hbr

/-- **`returnedKernel_not_identically_zero`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The returned
finite-conductor kernel is a genuinely nonzero object: there is an internal
`1000 < ℓ ≤ 5000` and an atom on which the local kernel does not vanish. -/
theorem returnedKernel_not_identically_zero :
    ∃ ell ∈ Finset.Icc 1001 5000, ∃ s z : ℤ, Kell ell s z ≠ 0 := by
  have hsq : Squarefree 1001 := by
    rw [show (1001 : ℕ) = 7 * (11 * 13) by norm_num, Nat.squarefree_mul_iff]
    refine ⟨by norm_num, Irreducible.squarefree
      (Nat.irreducible_iff_prime.mpr (Nat.prime_iff.mp (by norm_num))), ?_⟩
    rw [Nat.squarefree_mul_iff]
    exact ⟨by norm_num,
      Irreducible.squarefree (Nat.irreducible_iff_prime.mpr (Nat.prime_iff.mp (by norm_num))),
      Irreducible.squarefree (Nat.irreducible_iff_prime.mpr (Nat.prime_iff.mp (by norm_num)))⟩
  refine ⟨1001, by decide, (7 : ℤ), (7 : ℤ) + 1, ?_⟩
  exact Kell_ne_zero_at_prime_atom hsq (by decide) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

/-! ## §59.4  The exact-loop firewall -/

/-- Status tag for the reassembly route. -/
inductive LoopStatus
  | exactLoop
  | closure
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Reassembling the returned kernel into the original conductor expression. -/
def reassembleStatus : LoopStatus := .exactLoop

/-- **`reassembly_exact_loop`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` firewall (HIGH PRIORITY).  Reassembling the
returned finite-conductor kernel into the original conductor expression produces the
tautology `0 = 0` — an exact loop — while the returned kernel itself is not the zero object.
No closure is obtained by reassembly. -/
theorem reassembly_exact_loop :
    (∀ A B z : ℤ, returnedKernel A B z - returnedKernel A B z = 0) ∧
      reassembleStatus = LoopStatus.exactLoop ∧
      reassembleStatus ≠ LoopStatus.closure ∧
      (∃ ell ∈ Finset.Icc 1001 5000, ∃ s z : ℤ, Kell ell s z ≠ 0) :=
  ⟨fun A B z => sub_self _, rfl, by decide, returnedKernel_not_identically_zero⟩

end Effectivity
end Erdos287
